This research delivers an efficient predictive tool that reduces reliance on computationally expensive DFT calculations and accelerates alloy defect investigation. By addressing the gap in systematic interstitial-substitutional interaction models in HCP metals, this work enhances understanding of defect energetics and establishes a foundation for applications across broader crystal systems.

title: Achieving cryogenic strength-ductility synergy of near-α titanium alloy fabricated by laser direct energy deposition through multiscale deformation
abstract: • A novel cryogenic titanium alloy is fabricated via laser direct energy deposition. • The annealed alloy demonstrates an excellent strength-ductility synergy at 77 K. • Multiple twins accommodate dislocations and generate stress fields at interfaces. • Twins promote various slip systems activation and dislocations dissociation. A novel near-α titanium alloy designed for cryogenic applications was fabricated via laser direct energy deposition process. The microstructures and cryogenic mechanical properties of the alloy before and after heat treatment were analyzed. Both as-deposited and annealed alloys demonstrate remarkable strength-ductility synergy. Notably, the elongation of annealed alloy (∼17.5 %) is about 84.2 % higher than as-deposited alloy, while maintaining high ultimate tensile strength (∼1174 MPa). To comprehensively examine the impact of microstructure on cryogenic deformation, in-situ cryogenic TEM strain testing and other analytical techniques were employed, which offer new insights into the multiscale deformation mechanisms at cryogenic temperature. Larger α phase facilitates twin nucleation and effectively accommodates the strain gradient resulting from inhomogeneous deformation. Multiple twins promote non-basal dislocation slip and introduce additional heterogeneous interfaces, enhancing both twinning-induced plasticity and dynamic Hall-Petch effect. As flow stress increases, <c + a> dislocations near twins dissociate into <c> and dislocations, contributing to dislocation strengthening. The notable enlargement of grain size in annealed alloys facilitates more active dislocation behavior driven by extensive twinning, promoting sustained strain hardening. These findings not only elucidate the cryogenic deformation mechanism of near-α titanium alloy but also offer promising avenues for developing high-performance titanium alloys by additive manufacturing.

title: Perovskite solar cell efficiency prediction on the basis of structure of organic hole-transporting materials
abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs), particularly in the n-i-p architecture, require high-performance hole-transporting materials (HTMs). The rational design of HTMs demands a systematic understanding of structure–property relationships. Here, we analyze a dataset of cross-laboratory experimental results encompassing 177 peer-reviewed publications to decode the impact of an HTM structure on the device performance. Our correlation analysis reveals the fill factor (FF) as the most sensitive parameter for the HTM optimization, underscoring its critical role in efficiency enhancement. Through feature selection, we identify key predictors of device performance. These include nitrogen-containing functional groups (amide, imide, imine), carbonyl oxygen content, the count of aromatic and aliphatic carbo-/heterocycles, and van der Waals surface area descriptors. Using these insights, we develop a tree model-based stacked regressor that predicts device power conversion efficiency (PCE) with a root mean squared error (RMSE) as low as 2 %. This data-driven framework bridges molecular design with device physics and provides actionable guidelines for synthesizing next-generation HTMs via chemical space exploration.

title: Macroscopic self-assembly through electrostatic interactions controlled by CO2
abstract: • CO 2 -triggered modulation of macroscopic self-assembly behavior. • Under N 2 purging and heating at 80 °C, reversible self-assembly can be realized without replacing the solution • Quantitatively measured the relationship between the polymer structure and the ionic strength in the solution. CO 2 was strategically integrated into the electrostatic interaction driven macroscopic supramolecular assembly (MSA) as a dynamic regulator of electrostatic interactions between gels. The reversible assembly–disassembly transition was achieved through sequential CO 2 infusion and N 2 purging/heating, which highlighted the switchable and non-destructive nature of the process. This tunability originates from the CO 2 -responsive protonation–deprotonation equilibrium of dimethylethylamine (DMEA), which modulates the ionic strength of the medium and consequently shifts the electrostatic potential at the interface between gel and water. By quantitatively correlating gel surface charge density with DMEA concentration and employing a controllable centrifugal force method to measure electrostatic forces between gels, this study systematically elucidated how CO 2 -mediated ionic perturbations govern the hierarchical organization, packing density, and mechanical stability of the assembled network. These insights establish CO 2 as a versatile chemical stimulus for precision control of supramolecular architectures.

title: Orientation solidification map through laser scan strategy Engineering for additively manufactured stainless steels
abstract: • 3D finite element model links scan strategy to grain shape and orientation in LPBF 316L. • Melting modes (conduction, transition, keyhole) and remelting govern grain texture dynamics. • A solidification map links G × R to crystal orientation, enabling process control in LPBF. Using a three-dimensional multiphase finite element model combined with a multiscale characterization framework, this study investigates the solidification characteristics and grain orientations of 316L stainless steel (316LSS) during laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) under different laser scanning strategies. Three common patterns—meander, stripe, and chessboard—were evaluated to capture the associated thermal profiles and melt pool (MP) dynamics. While conduction dominated across all strategies, the stripe and chessboard patterns showed greater susceptibility to keyhole and transition melting modes. Thermal simulations revealed variations in remelting depth: the stripe pattern exhibited the deepest remelting (∼150 μm), while the meander pattern showed the shallowest (∼50 μm), influencing grain refinement and morphology. Crystallographic orientation analysis indicated that interactions between keyhole, transition, and conductive MPs altered preferred growth directions. The meander strategy promoted [101] and [111] orientations, whereas the stripe and chessboard strategies showed stronger alignment toward [111]. By correlating thermal parameters—temperature gradient (G) and solidification rate (R)—with local crystallographic orientation and grain structure, a solidification orientation map was developed. This map demonstrates how scan strategy–driven MP interactions control microstructural features, providing a predictive tool for grain morphology and texture design in LPBF-316LSS components.

title: Hierarchically aligned SiC whisker in polymer composites for enhancing mechanical and surface breakdown strength
abstract: Solid dielectrics are required for mechanical support and to separate the conductors in gas-insulated systems. However, electric field distortion at their triple junctions would cause surface breakdown. While incorporating inorganic fillers can mitigate this issue, conventional methods using randomly dispersed particles suffer from a critical trade-off between insulation performance and filler loading. Herein, DLP 3D printing is used to lay SiC whiskers (SiC w ) in a 2D polymer flat by designing a printing thickness smaller than the length of the whiskers. The resulting SiC w composites show randomly distributed SiC whiskers in the in-plane direction, and aligned SiC whiskers in the out-of-plane direction. We studied the positive effects of 2D-aligned SiC w composites on the mechanical and surface breakdown performances. Strong anisotropy in the mechanical strength was observed with the tensile strength of 82 MPa in the in-plane direction versus that of 48 MPa in the out-of-plane-90° direction at the SiC loading of 6 wt%. More importantly, the out-of-plane oriented SiC w composites exhibit a higher surface flashover voltage than that of the in-plane oriented ones, in which the flashover voltage of the 4 wt% SiC w composites in out-of-plane-90° direction is 38 % higher than that of pure resin. Applying the DLP 3D printing technique to orient 1D fillers in polymer is of great significance for enhancing the reliability of electrical equipment.

title: Multifunctional carbon dots promote post-extraction bone regeneration for alveolar ridge preservation
abstract: PG-CDs prepared from hydrothermal approach exhibit excellent performance to extraction socket healing based on the multifunctional illustration. • Guanidylated carbon dots (PG-CDs) with multifunction were synthesized via a controllably hydrothermal method. • PG-CDs combat pathogens containing Streptococcus mutans and MRSA via membrane-disruptive mechanism. • PG-CDs exhibit appreciable osteoinductive potential and immunomodulatory effects. • PG-CDs demonstrate effective prevention of bacterial infection and promotion of bone healing in extraction sockets. • PG-CDs offer a promising strategy for post-extraction healing and long-term ridge preservation. The extraction of a non-restorable tooth, required due to severe caries, periodontitis, or trauma, is a common precursor to dental implantation. Following tooth extraction, physiological bone resorption occurs, and even infections can disrupt the immune microenvironment, further exacerbating bone loss. Some approaches with sophisticated antibacterial and immunomodulatory functions are required to prevent infection and orchestrate favorable tissue regeneration. Herein, guanidylated carbon dots (PG-CDs) with stable physicochemical properties and antibacterial–immunomodulatory functions were synthesized via a controllably hydrothermal method using citric acid and polyhexamethylene guanidine (PHMG) as precursors. PG-CDs possessed uniform spherical morphology, and surface functional groups including –NH 2 and guanidyl moieties. PG-CDs displayed potent efficacy against a broad spectrum of bacteria containing oral bacteria and their biofilms via membrane disruption, coupled with high stability and little risk of resistance development. The PG-CDs possessed biocompatibility and effectively promoted a pro-regenerative microenvironment by accelerating osteogenic differentiation and guiding macrophage polarization towards the M2 phenotype. In vivo results further implied that PG-CDs effectively enhanced bone regeneration, effectively reduced oral pathogenic bacterial load, and facilitated extraction socket healing. Collectively, these findings suggest that PG-CDs represent a promising nanomedicine for maintaining alveolar bone height post-extraction and offer an effective therapeutic strategy for bone tissue regeneration.

title: Microstructural evolution and mechanical properties of CuSn5 processed by HPT followed by short-time annealing
abstract: • Grain growth behavior of ultrafine-grained Cu-5 wt% Sn was systematically studied. • Sn atoms preferentially segregate at general high-angle grain boundaries. • No detectable Sn segregation was found at LAGBs and CSL boundaries. • Grain boundary segregation and relaxation enhanced Vickers hardness after low temperature annealing. Nanocrystalline and ultrafine-grained metallic materials have received considerable attention in recent years due to their ultrahigh strength and unique mechanical properties. However, pure nanocrystalline metals exhibit thermal instability, making them prone to grain growth during thermal treatment and usage, which in turn reduces hardness and strength, and compromises their structural integrity. To improve the thermal stability of these materials, grain boundary segregation of solute elements has emerged as a promising approach. In this study, we used advanced scanning transmission electron microscopy to investigate the grain growth mechanisms of ultrafine-grained Cu-5 wt% Sn annealed at temperatures up to 350 °C. Our results indicate that Sn preferentially segregates at general high-angle GBs, while low-angle and coincidence site lattice GBs do not exhibit detectable enrichment of Sn. The segregation at these high angle GBs and GB relaxation explains the increased Vickers hardness of the Cu-Sn alloy during annealing.

title: Predicting paint resistance to pull-off by first principles calculations: The case of acrylic acid on (oxidised) metals
abstract: Paints are essential in everyday applications since they provide protective functions beyond aesthetics, such as corrosion resistance, UV shielding, and thermal performance enhancement. Adhesion is a critical factor governing the durability and performance of paints, yet the mechanisms controlling it at the atomic scale remain poorly understood. Here, we show that density functional theory (DFT) calculations can complement empirical adhesion tests and support the rational design of paint–substrate systems. We considered acrylic acid (a key component of acrylic paint) on pure and oxidised metallic substrates, including aluminium, iron, steel, alumina, hematite and goethite. The calculated adsorption energies and pull-off forces were compared with experimental paint breaking stress. The results show that acrylic acid binds more strongly to pristine metals than to oxides, and more in general the trends obtained across the considered substrates were in excellent agreement with the experiments, thereby establishing a quantitative correlation between molecular adsorption and macroscopic paint scratch. This approach offers a transferable route to design tailored coating–substrate systems, supporting applications in substrate protection and durability. • DFT pull-off forces reproduce experimental trends: DFT used to predict paint adhesion. • Substrate oxidation weakens acrylic acid binding, reducing adhesion. • Highest adhesion on stainless-steel due to molecule interaction with Cr and C atoms.

title: Structured approach towards surface feature classification on DED-printed parts
abstract: Highlights • Nomenclatures and classifications for systematic unequivocal labelling of surface features and defects for component specification and defect assessment are provided. • The key to comprehensive structured quantitative assessment of geometric features and defects of components made using directed energy deposition is application of a low-pass geometry filter to scanned data of such components. • Filtering of 3D geometry data on DED component enables quantitative assessment of large scale deviations as well as local features by means of computation of the local spatial distance to the filtered geometry. • The effective wall thickness computed from the filtered data provides a moving average for local assessment as well as statistical information of the thickness distribution of the component or a relevant section of it. Directed Energy Deposition is a proven technology for the economic production of medium to large sized metal structures. The process results in a characteristic surface structure composed of the molten layers. It is evident that, the surface structure impairs the strength of the workpiece during static and cyclic loading. Consequently, surface topology evaluation is crucial in the assessment of workpieces manufactured by Directed Energy Deposition. In this paper, methods for assessment and specification of workpieces are presented. First, a structured feature table is proposed, which allows the unambiguous and technical specification of surface features. Second, a workflow using a geometry filter on scanned final product data for the assessment of macro workpiece deviations and local features is presented and applied on exemplary workpieces. The exemplary results are critically reviewed in context to industrial application.

title: Cooling rate–mediated evolution of lamellar α colony microtexture in a near-α titanium alloy during β processing
abstract: • Cooling rate alone does not control α-colony microtexture formation; it is governed by prior β state. • Textured β grains promote aligned α-colony microtexture, whereas recrystallized β results in random orientations. • Double-colony formation is governed by β grain orientation matching, with minimal influence from cooling rate. • Heavy β deformation followed by intermediate cooling yields fine, non-bridged α colonies with minimal microtexture. This study systematically investigates how cooling rate mediates the evolution of lamellar α colony microtextured regions (MTRs) in a near-α titanium alloy during β processing. The initial MTRs formed after β processing can be inherited into subsequent processing steps, critically influencing dwell-fatigue life. To address this, two β processing routes—β deformation only (β-Def) versus β deformation plus β annealing (β-Def + HT)—were compared, with samples cooled from the β phase at rates between 2 and 0.125 °C/s. In the β-Def route, slower cooling (0.125 vs 2 °C/s) nearly doubled the mean α colony MTR size and significantly coarsened prior β grains. Conversely, the β-Def + HT route showed only a modest increase in MTR size under slow cooling. The β-Def route introduced an intragranular transformation texture (<11–20 > α), while complete β recrystallization in the β-Def + HT route randomized the MTR orientations. Double-colony MTRs (paired colonies spanning special β grain boundaries) formed only in β-Def at the slowest cooling rate, but occurred across all cooling rates in β-Def + HT, indicating that prior β crystallography governs double-colony formation. An optimized processing strategy using β deformation with an intermediate cooling rate (∼0.25 °C/s) produced relatively small (∼150 μm), randomly oriented α colonies without double-colony MTRs.

title: High heating rate effects in sintering: A phase-field study of La-doped alumina
abstract: Sintering is a widespread manufacturing process, accounting for a significant portion of global energy expenditure. However, controlling this process has been mostly a trial-and-error process, being costly in both time and money. The recent advance of high heating rate sintering methods, which promise higher energy efficiency and better properties, only adds to this. This paper aims to reduce these costs by shedding light on the microstructural evolution during high heating rate sintering, which will allow for quicker parameter optimization and improved properties. The focus will be on how a representative microstructure changes locally as well as globally while resolving grains and the green body at scale, which no prior paper has done. A representative multiphysics phase-field solver is employed, incorporating a novel particle-based temperature model, which recovered many characteristics typical of high heating rate sintering. Comparing the simulation data to experimental data showed reasonable agreement over a large density range without parameter adjustment. Furthermore, the advance of a sintering front including grain growth effects could be shown simulatively for the first time in literature. These findings suggest that the model can be used for the design of practical heating schedules for the sintering of novel materials. • A novel multiphysics phase-field model of sintering accounting for temperature, applicable to any metal and/or ceramic materials system is presented. • A novel particle-based temperature model allows efficient upscaling to the parts scale and reduces time integration effort. • Many characteristics of high heating rate sintering are recovered & simulated densification rates are shown capable of matching experiments. • Green bodies with Biot numbers below 0.017 can be assumed homogeneous in both temperature and microstructure. • Green bodies with higher Biot number were observed to develop sintering fronts, which can be exploited to still obtain homogeneous microstructures from temporary inhomogeneous evolution.

title: Simultaneous photo-magnetic dual hyperthermia combined with radiotherapy enhanced by snowman‑shaped Janus nanoparticles in CT26 colon cancer model
abstract: • Snowman-shaped Janus nanoparticles enable targeted magnetic tumor delivery. • Combined photo-magnetic hyperthermia and radiotherapy significantly reduce colon tumor growth. • Nanoparticles enhance MRI imaging and show excellent biocompatibility. • Dual therapy elevates VEGF and Hsp70, improving treatment efficacy and survival. Colon cancer is the third most common malignant tumor worldwide with high mortality. This study developed snowman-shaped Janus nanoparticles (JNPs) (Fe 3 O 4 -Au@poly(NIPAAm-co-AAM-co-AA)) for targeted cancer therapy by combining photomagnetic hyperthermia and radiotherapy. JNPs were synthesized and characterized using TEM and SEM, confirming their size (85.3 ± 4.1 nm). Cytotoxicity on CT26 cells was evaluated via MTT assay. Cellular uptake, in vivo biodistribution, and potential hepatic damage were evaluated through ICP-OES and liver enzyme measurements. MRI was utilized to study tumor targeting, while temperature changes laser exposure, and alternating magnetic field (AMF) conditions were monitored using an IR camera. Western blotting assessed Hsp70, and VEGF protein expression. In addition, histological examination, tumor volume, and survival time in CT26 colon tumor-bearing mice were monitored to assess the antitumor efficacy of the JNPs. The JNPs demonstrated good hemocompatibility and effective magnetic tumor targeting in MRI studies. In vivo experiments showed significant tumor volume reduction and increased Hsp70 and VEGF expression in mice treated with the combination of JNPs, radiotherapy, and concurrent AMF and NIR hyperthermia (p < 0.0001). The JNPs are promising as multifunctional platforms for cancer therapy, demonstrating excellent biocompatibility, magnetic targeting, and enhanced hyperthermia and radiotherapy, which may improve treatment outcomes in targeted multimodal cancer therapies.

title: Microstructural evolution, deformation modes, and failure mechanisms in laser powder bed fusion processed nickel-free and 316L stainless steels
abstract: • Microstructure and failure behaviors of additive manufactured Ni-free steel. • Ni-free steel had highest hardness but low strength and brittle fracture. • Heat treatment induced duplex structure, enhanced ductility and mixed fracture mode. • Chi promoted cracking and formed boundaries increased plasticity localization. This study investigates the influence of microstructures on mechanical behavior and failure mechanisms of laser based powder bed fusion processed nickel-free and 316L stainless steels using small punch testing, nanoindentation, and miniaturized tensile testing. The as-printed 316L with a fully austenitic structure and high-density dislocation cells exhibited a nanohardness of 3.0 GPa, tensile strength of 600 MPa, and elongation close to 60 %, with failure occurring through ductile microvoid coalescence. In contrast, the as-printed nickel-free stainless steel with a fully ferritic matrix and random dislocation networks showed a high nanohardness of 4.94 GPa, but poor ductility of 2 % and transgranular cleavage fracture. Heat treatment at 950 °C for 30 min transformed the nickel-free steel into a duplex microstructure (56 % ferrite and 41 % austenite, with a minor 3 % Chi phase), reducing dislocation density and inducing stacking faults. This resulted in moderate improvement in tensile strength as well as ductility and a mixed fracture mode. Post-mortem analysis revealed that Chi phase assisted crack initiation and strain localization was observed near coarse grains. The evolution of low-angle to high-angle grain and twin boundaries promoted plastic deformation. These results highlight the importance of phase engineering and microstructural control in optimizing the ductility and toughness of nickel-free steels.

title: Strain visualization of DED 316 steel via Digital image correlation and Fourier Transform analysis: effects of hydrogen and heat treatment
abstract: • Hydrogen embrittlement (HE) sensitivity was reduced for AM-DED 316 by heat treatment. • Heat treatment induced microstructural changes and reduced 2 types of dislocation and density via 3 comparative methods. • Dynamic strain evolution was analyzed by DIC, and 2D Fourier Transform was performed to study the Strain-frequency ratio. This study investigates the influence of heat treatment at different temperatures (600, 800, and 1200 °C) on the microstructure, dislocation stability, and element segregation of 316L stainless steel fabricated by direct energy deposition. To understand how these changes affect hydrogen embrittlement resistance and the mechanical properties of the samples, tensile testing and digital image correlation (DIC) were employed to examine the strain/instability evolution under combined conditions after heat treatment and hydrogen charging. Results show that dislocation densities decreased after heat treatment, which in turn increased the hydrogen embrittlement resistance of samples with emergence of recrystallization and twin grains. DIC revealed that heat-treated samples exhibited more strain hotspots, which initiated and developed more extensively compared to as-received (AR) samples. In comparison, AR samples showed fewer sites of strain accumulation, leading to wider crack propagation and earlier failure. Hydrogen-charged specimens exhibited narrower strain ranges and more localized strain distributions, indicating a shift toward brittle fracture behavior. In contrast, hydrogen-free samples exhibited higher mean magnitude values and spatial variation across the range of spatial frequencies, as confirmed by two-dimensional Fourier Transform analysis. The methods and analyses in this paper provide a new perspective on evaluating hydrogen embrittlement via demystifying strain/instability evolution.

title: Optimizing permeability of microporous scaffolds through CFD simulation to enhance osseointegration
abstract: Permeability, as an important structural parameter, has not been thoroughly validated for its role in osseointegration, and the optimal range of permeability for osseointegration remains undefined. This study utilized computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation to design scaffolds and calculate permeability and fluid velocity within the scaffold structure. A series of microporous scaffolds with controlled permeability gradients were fabricated using selective laser melting (SLM). These scaffolds were implanted into rabbit distal femurs, and Osseointegration was evaluated via micro-CT analysis 8 weeks post-surgery. The results indicated that the optimal permeability range for osteogenesis was between 8.82E-08 m2 and 1.28E-07 m2, which is higher than the permeability of human bone trabeculae. We also preliminarily discussed the influence of flow velocity on osteogenesis. This study combined in vivo experiments with CFD, using permeability as the primary parameter for experimental research, providing new theoretical basis for the design of bone scaffolds in the future.

title: Experimental study on the tensile properties of composites with Cr20Ni80 TFP electric heating layer under energization
abstract: • Glass/epoxy laminates built-in Cr20Ni80 TFP electric heating layer could be applied to aircraft electrothermal anti-icing/de-icing systems. • The electrothermal composites could achieve average heating rate of 0.7 °C/s in 20 s at the power density of 0.6 W·cm −2 . • The retention rates of tensile strength and modulus of electrothermal composites under energization are at least 82.51% and 76.54%. Polymer composites embedded with a lightweight electric heating layer show great potential for application in aircraft inlet anti-icing/de-icing systems. The mechanical properties of such electrothermal composites are critical to flight reliability. The tensile properties of glass/epoxy composites incorporating a Cr20Ni80 tailored fiber placement (TFP) electric heating layer under energization were investigated. For the middle layer, three different Cr20Ni80 wire spacings on the TFP fabrics were designed to meet the power density requirement of 0.6 W·cm −2 . The composites achieved an average heating rate of 0.7 °C/s during the initial 20 s. An integrated approach combining digital image correlation (DIC) and infrared thermography was employed to monitor the tensile displacement field and surface temperature distribution of samples simultaneously during energization-tensile testing. The tensile strength and elastic modulus of composite samples with a wire spacing of 10 mm were 18.88 % and 35.01 % higher than those with a 6 mm spacing, respectively. Compared to non-energized counterparts, the energized samples maintained high retention rates of at least 82.51 % for tensile strength and 76.54 % for elastic modulus. Damage morphology analysis indicates that energization induces interfacial debonding of both glass fibers and Cr20Ni80 wires from the epoxy matrix, accompanied by matrix cracking and delamination.

title: Support-free fabrication of IN625 low-angle overhang structures using laser powder bed fusion (LPBF)
abstract: Support-free IN625 overhang bars (60 × 10 × 7 mm 3 ) were successfully fabricated using laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), achieving a minimum overhang angle of 5° at 30 µm layer thickness and 10° at 60 µm layer thickness. Supported bars were also fabricated to conduct a systematic comparison. Residual stress analysis revealed an increase in residual stresses with decreasing overhang angles. The downskin surface topography exhibited pronounced stair-stepping effects and powder adhesion, especially at low angles. Microstructural characterization confirmed columnar grains spread through the bulk region and small equiaxed grains in the downskin region of the low-overhang angle bars. While the primary dendrite arm spacing remained consistent within the bulk, it increased in the downskin region due to reduced heat dissipation. Correspondingly, the micro-hardness remains consistent in the bulk region, it decreases in the downskin region for the overhang angles below 30°. Uniaxial-tensile tests demonstrate consistent strength, while elongation is higher for increased overhang angle.

title: Tensile behavior of SiCf/Ti60 composites at RT and 600 °C
abstract: • The prepared SiC f /Ti60 composite exhibits excellent tensile properties, with tensile strengths exceeding 1300 MPa at both room temperature and 600 °C. • The RT fracture process of SiC f /Ti60 composites is as follows: RL fracture → RL cracks penetrating the matrix → matrix cracks causing fiber instability fracture → final capsule fracture. • The 600 °C fracture process of SiC f /Ti60 composites is as follows: RL fracture → matrix plasticity increases, fibers fracture first → RL cracks penetrate the matrix → final capsule fracture. • Residual tensile stress is the primary cause of initial failure at the interface between amorphous carbon/TiC. In this study, continuous SiC fibers reinforced Ti60 (SiC f /Ti60) composites were prepared by the method of coating fibers with matrix and hot isostatic pressing (HIP). The SiC f /Ti60 composites showed excellent tensile properties at room temperature (RT) and 600 °C, with a tensile strength of over 1300 MPa. The fracture process of the composites at different temperatures was studied using XRD, SEM, EBSD, and TEM techniques. The results showed that the RT fracture process of the SiC f /Ti60 composites was: reaction layer (RL) fracture → RL cracks penetrating into the matrix → matrix cracks causing fiber instability fracture → final capsule fracture. The high-temperature fracture process of the SiC f /Ti60 composites was: RL fracture → matrix plasticity increases, fibers fracture first → RL cracks penetrate into the matrix → final capsule fracture. The failure of the RL at RT and 600 °C primarily occurred at the interface of amorphous carbon/TiC, which is related to the residual stress at the interface. The nucleation and propagation of the matrix cracks are related to the distance from the failure position of the RL and the basal and prismatic Schmid factors

title: Signatures of magnetic and topological hall effects in Mn2BiSbTe5: an anomalous low-temperature transition
abstract: We report Mn2BiSbTe5 as a new magnetic topological insulator (MTIs), expanding the Mn-based tetradymite family of MTIs. Single-crystal growth and systematic characterization reveal its intrinsic structural, magnetic, and electronic properties. Raman spectroscopy identifies distinct vibrational modes, while X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) confirms the valence states of individual atoms. Magneto-transport and magnetization measurements uncover a magnetic transition below 20 K, accompanied by a sharp anomaly in the temperature derivative of the magnetic moment, suggesting long-range magnetic ordering. A notable bifurcation between zero-field-cooled (ZFC) and field-cooled (FC) magnetization hints at spin-glass-like behavior or competing magnetic interactions. Furthermore, Hall measurements provide evidence of a topological Hall effect (THE), highlighting the coupling between magnetism and topology. The tunable magnetic ordering in Mn2BiSbTe5 offers a new avenue for engineering axion insulator (AxI) phases, anomalous quantum Hall effect (AQHE), and THE, making it a strong candidate for next-generation spintronic and quantum electronic applications. These findings pave the way for the design of novel magnetic topological materials with tailored quantum properties.

title: Enhanced ductility by stress confinement in multilayered glassy thin films
abstract: • Nano-structuring metallic glass thin film triggers synergistic effect of enhanced plasticity without compromising strength. • Strong stress confinement to 100 nm revealed by 4D-STEM strain mapping. • Structural confinement of stress and enhanced plasticity were confirmed via MD simulations. • Plasticity improvement by designed microstructural features at the length scale of 100 nm. The deformation of metallic glasses (MGs) is characterized by strong strain localizations in shear bands and rapid propagation thereof, leading to brittle fracture. The incorporation of secondary phases or heterogeneities into the glassy structure has been shown to enhance ductility, resulting in the formation of metallic glass composites (MGCs). In this study, we examine the deformation behavior of MGCs composed of two distinct glassy phases applying in-situ deformation combined with 4D scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM). Local strain evolution was tracked during loading and revealed that nanolayered MGCs exhibit significantly enhanced plasticity compared to monolithic glasses. This improvement of ductility was attributed to a notable confinement of atomic strain in the soft layer, which is enabled by the layered architecture. Notably, confining stress within individual layers suppresses the development of mature shear bands and delays the onset of critical shear instabilities. Complementary molecular dynamics simulations support experimental results, clarifying how architectural confinement and phase synergy can be utilized to enhance the mechanical properties of two-phase glassy materials.

title: Research on the influence of different heat treatment methods on the performance of titanium alloy (TC4) fasteners
abstract: • This study innovatively introduces a mid-process oxygen injection mechanism to accurately simulate actual heat treatment conditions. • Adding a baffle during heat treatment promotes the formation of an oxide layer. • Adding an insulation layer during heat treatment reduces the thickness of the oxide layer. • Adding an insulation layer during heat treatment improves the shear performance of the material. The heat treatment of alloys directly determines their final properties. This research designed four differentiated heat treatment methods and systematically analysed the mechanical properties, microstructure and surface colour of the materials. Combined with molecular dynamics, the mechanical properties and oxygen atom implantation mechanism on Ti-6Al-4 V (TC4) fastener performance were explored during heat treatment. Research results show that TC4 alloy would be aggregated, grew and precipitated equiaxed α phase, that would be distribution like chains and show golden surface after adding insulation. It is because the number of decomposed O atoms is decreased that would be led to reduce bonds probability such as Ti-O or O-O, which would effectively hinder the oxidation. It would be enforced the shear performance but the strength, plasticity and fatigue properties are also affected litter. With the baffle is added into system, it can decompose more O atoms and oxide layer would be thick, and surface shown blue-purple or gray-blue. Adding an insulation layer or baffle can make the oxide layer uniformity. Furthermore, this research provides a new simulation method for mid-way injection of oxygen atoms for TC4 or other materials during heat treatment. Experiments and engineering cases have verified the reliability of this method.

title: Polymeric-filled alumina ceramics with enhanced fracture toughness
abstract: Ceramics’ toughening mechanisms have been an area of focus for many researchers. Although intrinsic toughening mechanisms reduce the need for a secondary structure, their performance has not yet matched that of extrinsic toughening mechanisms. This study investigates the mechanical properties of alumina ceramics filled with an epoxy matrix, prepared through a capillary suspension method. The method to fabricate the ceramics and corresponding composites is straightforward and scalable. Mechanical testing, including single-edge notch bending (SENB) and flexural tests, demonstrated significant improvements in fracture toughness, Young’s modulus, and tensile strength for the composite compared to porous ceramics and pure epoxy. The fracture toughness of 12 MPa m for 45 % Al 2 O 3 surpasses that reported in literature generally, and particularly for an equivalent density. SEM analyses identified primary toughening mechanisms such as particle pullout, crack deflection, and limited crack bridging. The density-normalized analysis highlighted the composite’s superior specific mechanical performance, emphasizing its potential for structural applications where the strength-to-weight ratio is critical.

title: Multifunctional mussel-inspired gelatin methacryloyl hydrogels for infection-sensitive applications
abstract: Bacterial infections remain a major health concern, with early and accessible detection critical for effective intervention. Here, we introduce a multifunctional and biocompatible gelatin methacryloyl hydrogel designed for real-time visual monitoring and localized antimicrobial action. The system incorporates bromothymol blue (BTB) encapsulated within pH-responsive smart pigments, enabling a controlled colorimetric shift from yellow to blue in response to basic microenvironments generated by Gram-negative bacteria. In vitro studies using Escherichia coli validate the platform’s utility for rapid infection detection. Catechol functionalization enhances the hydrogel’s mechanical strength and mussel-inspired adhesion, supporting appropriate contact with infection-prone surfaces. As a proof of concept for therapeutic integration, zinc oxide (ZnO) nanoparticles were embedded to demonstrate the hydrogel’s capacity for antimicrobial agent loading and release. This integrated, easy-to-use material provides a promising strategy for simultaneous detection and treatment of bacterial infections, especially in resource-limited or point-of-care settings.

title: Multi-length scale multi-material topology optimization: A CAMP approach to handling overfilling constraints
abstract: Avoiding infeasible phase mixtures and ensuring minimum feature sizes are critical in multi-material topology optimization for additive manufacturing. Yet, these requirements introduce numerous local overfilling constraints that are prohibitively expensive to handle with gradient-based optimization. Conventional aggregation methods reduce this burden but yield inaccurate constraint estimates, risk numerical oscillations, and are incompatible with efficient algorithms such as the optimality criteria (OC) method. We propose the Constraints Adjusted Material with Penalization (CAMP) method, which implicitly enforces local overfilling constraints through constraint transformation and stiffness reinterpolation. CAMP overcomes the drawbacks of aggregation methods, eliminates the computational burden associated with handling massive numbers of constraints, and enables the use of OC solvers for the first time in multi-material topology optimization to provide synergistic control of multi-material length scales and phase mixing. Numerical studies on 2D and 3D minimum compliance problems with volume and manufacturing cost constraints demonstrate that the proposed method ensures independent minimum length scales, suppresses phase mixing at material interfaces, and achieves up to a 10 × speedup over traditional algorithms. Furthermore, the cost-constrained designs outperform volume-constrained solutions, underscoring their practical value for manufacturability-driven multi-material design. • We propose a CAMP-based multi-material topology optimization framework to handle local overfilling constraints. • CAMP minimizes phase mixing even at material interfaces. • The framework supports independent minimum length scales, allowing resolution-specific customization for additive manufacturing. • We apply the optimality criteria method, for the first time, to multi-length-scale and multi-material topology optimization. • We solve volume and cost-constrained problems with millions of design variables and overfilling constraints efficiently on a standard laptop.

title: Enhanced polymer melt flow control in material extrusion: modified cross-WLF modeling and experimental validation of nozzle design for pressure reduction
abstract: Material extrusion additive manufacturing performance critically depends on polymer melt flow dynamics within the nozzle, yet current viscosity models miss to accurately capture solid-to-liquid phase transitions during processing. This study presents a modified Cross-Williams-Landel-Ferry (Cross-WLF) viscosity model incorporating a hyperbolic tangent melt fraction function to address glass transition effects and numerical stability. The enhanced model was implemented through finite element analysis to compare conventional single-channel nozzle designs with innovative tri-channel splitting geometries. Experimental validation using a custom force measurement apparatus demonstrated high agreement between theoretical predictions and measured extrusion forces across temperatures from 200°C to 250°C. The tri-channel nozzle design achieved a remarkable 66.5% pressure reduction compared to conventional designs while maintaining superior thermal stability and flow uniformity at feed rates up to 15 mm/s. Statistical analysis revealed no significant differences between predicted and experimental forces, validating the model's predictive capability. These findings enable optimized nozzle design for enhanced printing speeds and reduced mechanical stress on extruder systems, advancing the efficiency of the material extrusion process.

title: Elastic deformation suppresses ion demixing in mixed-halide perovskites
abstract: We simulated the kinetics of ion demixing in mixed-halide perovskites using phenomenological Cahn-Hilliard equation. In the model we considered the chemical and the elastic part of Helmholtz free energy of the perovskite lattice, as well as the effect of free carriers generated by sample illumination. If the demixing process is accompanied by local elastic deformation caused by the dependence of the lattice parameter on the local chemical composition, the elastic contribution to the free energy is larger than the other two parts so that elastic deformation effectively suppresses the ion segregation. The demixing can take place if the internal stresses are relieved by surface elastic relaxation, or if the deformation of the lattice is plastic like around structure defects or at grain boundaries. • Spontaneous ion demixing in mixed-halide perovskites is simulated using phenomenological Cahn-Hilliard equation. • The model includes elastic deformation and free carriers created by light absorption. • From the simulation it follows that elastic deformation effectively hinders the demixing process. • The demixing take place only if the deformation is relaxed, for instance, at a rough surface or due to structure defects.

title: Integrated experimental and numerical investigation of fracture onset in automotive components using finite element analysis
abstract: • Hybrid digital image correlation-finite element method quantifies fracture in full-scale brake caliper parts. • Virtual path generation enables model calibration with limited test data. • Hosford-Coulomb parameters optimized via two cost function strategies. • Diverse specimen designs achieve broad stress triaxiality coverage. This study proposes a robust and application-oriented methodology for calibrating plastic and fracture properties of various materials used in automotive brake calipers, components often constrained by complex geometries and pre-straining histories. Recognizing the challenges in traditional fracture testing due to limited specimen feasibility, we propose a two-tier calibration strategy: a conventional hybrid experimental–numerical approach utilizing notched fracture specimens, and a virtual path generation method based on the Rice–Tracey model for geometrically constrained components. The virtual path approach employs both fracture strain and damage indicator cost functions to ensure robust parameter identification under non-proportional loading conditions. Calibrated Hosford–Coulomb models were validated through tensile and V-bending simulations, showing that even in the absence of diverse fracture specimens, the virtual path method achieves predictive accuracy comparable to conventional techniques. More importantly, the proposed framework enables reliable fracture parameter calibration directly from component-level geometries, thereby bridging the gap between material characterization and structural application. This methodology offers a scalable and versatile tool for integrating ductile fracture models into automotive design, ultimately enhancing the reliability and performance of safety–critical components

title: Optimizing shape memory performance in 4D-printed PLA hinges: An integrated study on geometry and process parameter effects
abstract: 4D additive manufacturing (AM) enhances the capabilities of 3D printed structures by enabling them to change shape in response to external stimuli. However, the lack of optimized geometric and processing parameters remains a key barrier to fully unlocking the potential of this technology. Therefore, this study investigates foldable hinges, critical components in 4D smart structures that enable the complex deformations required for folding and deployment. We focus on the shape memory performance of polylactic acid (PLA) hinges fabricated using fused deposition modeling (FDM). Our research examines how various geometric and processing parameters influence the recovery behavior of foldable hinges. Key factors such as hinge thickness, length, printing speed, and training temperature are assessed for their impact on recovery ratio and lifespan. To analyze the relationships between these variables and shape memory performance, we also developed a regression model, enhancing the reliability of FDM-fabricated PLA hinges. The results provide valuable insights for designing high-performance components for 4DAM applications, emphasizing the need for integrating design, materials, and process optimization. Furthermore, the optimized hinge design demonstrates actuation in an origami-inspired deployable structure, showcasing its promising potential for aerospace applications.

title: Sustainable nanoarchitectonics of cellulose-derived spherical activated carbon for efficient uremic toxin removal in pharmaceutical applications
abstract: • Cellulose-derived spherical carbons (SACs) synthesized via steam activation. • SAC100 achieved 2334 m 2 g −1 area and 762 mg g −1 indole uptake, exceeding Kremezin®. • High selectivity retained for α-amylase and β-aminoisobutyric acid. • Cellulose-derived SACs provide sustainable, biocompatible CKD therapy option. Activated carbon adsorbents are essential in pharmaceutical applications for removing uremic toxins in chronic kidney disease (CKD) patients. However, commercial petroleum-based products such as AST-120 (Kremezin®) require high dosages (2 g, three times daily) and face limited patient compliance. In this study, spherical activated carbons were synthesized from renewable microcrystalline cellulose via direct carbonization and steam activation under optimized conditions. The resulting materials retained uniform spherical morphology and exhibited hierarchical pore structures. The smaller-precursor carbon exhibited a BET surface area of 2,334 m 2 g −1 , high carbon purity (96.3 %), and superior adsorption performance, achieving an indole uptake of 762.2 mg g −1 , exceeding that of Kremezin® (637.1 mg g −1 ). It further showed enhanced selectivity, retaining 81.3 % of α-amylase and 91.7 % of DL-β-aminoisobutyric acid in solution. Selectivity indices reached up to 95.28, indicating effective discrimination between toxins and essential biomolecules. These findings highlight the potential of cellulose-derived spherical carbons as high-performance, biocompatible alternatives for oral adsorbent therapies. Their enhanced adsorption capacity, reduced non-specific interactions, and sustainable origin support their applicability in next-generation CKD treatment platforms, potentially contributing to improved patient compliance.

title: Engineering magnetoactive 3D CZFO/PVDF composites scaffolds with bioelectrical responsiveness for bone tissue regeneration
abstract: The growing incidence of bone-related pathologies has intensified the demand for advanced strategies in bone tissue repair. Among these, physical stimulation, particularly mechanical and electrical cues, has emerged as a promising approach to promote tissue regeneration. In this work, three-dimensional (3D) electroactive scaffolds were developed to mimic the natural bone microenvironment and support MC3T3-E1 preosteoblast adhesion and proliferation. The scaffolds were fabricated using a sacrificial molding technique, in which 3D-printed polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) molds were filled with a solution of poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) and magnetostrictive Co 0 . 5 Zn 0 . 5 Fe 2 O 4 (CZFO) nanoparticles. After solvent evaporation, the PVA mold was fully dissolved, yielding highly porous scaffolds with architecture replicating the original mold. Structural and biological assessments demonstrated successful cell proliferation at both the surface and within the scaffold, with no evidence of cytotoxicity. Furthermore, dynamic magnetoelectrical stimulation, applied via a custom-designed magnetic bioreactor, significantly enhanced cell adhesion and proliferation compared to non-stimulated conditions after 72 h. These findings highlight the potential of magnetoactive 3D composite scaffolds as functional platforms for bone tissue engineering.

title: Assessment of physicochemical properties and biological responses of chemically surface-modified microcapsules for self-healing dental restorative materials
abstract: • Melamine increased formaldehyde release, shown by a newly refined Purpald assay. • Melamine improved capsule strength and integrity under functionalization procedures. • Capsules functionalization improved thermal, mechanical, and biological performance. • Formaldehyde levels were safe; cytotoxicity came from early core release • Future work should target capsule stability over reducing formaldehyde. Approximately 50% of resin-based dental restorations fail within ten years, mainly due to secondary caries and material fractures. Incorporating self-healing microcapsules containing resin-based agents that polymerize upon release offers a promising strategy to repair microcracks and extend restoration longevity. Poly(urea–formaldehyde) (PUF) microcapsules are commonly used, but formaldehyde cytotoxicity remains a concern. This study developed alternative microcapsules by integrating melamine into the polymeric shell (PUMF) and functionalizing surfaces with methacrylate (TMSPM) or thiol (MPTMS) silanes, with or without a TEOS pre-coating, to reduce formaldehyde release and enhance biocompatibility. Microcapsules were synthesized via double-emulsion, encapsulating triethylene glycol dimethacrylate (TEGDMA), and characterized for morphology, mechanical stability, functionalization efficiency, formaldehyde release, and cytotoxicity. Melamine increased mechanical and morphological stability, surface roughness, and core retention, especially under functionalization, but also raised formaldehyde release in unmodified capsules. Functionalization with TMSPM and MPTMS significantly reduced formaldehyde release from both PUF and PUMF capsules. Metabolic assays showed dental pulp stem cells were more sensitive to TEGDMA, while fibroblasts were affected by TEGDMA combined with prolonged formaldehyde exposure. Overall, melamine-reinforced functionalized microcapsules exhibit improved stability, controlled formaldehyde release, and enhanced biocompatibility, supporting their potential as next-generation self-healing dental materials.

title: Extracting flow curves from spherical nanoindentation: The case of supercrystalline nanocomposites
abstract: • Spherical indentation-based method for the extraction of uniaxial stress–strain curves solely from nanoindentation data. • Applied to extract the flow curves of supercrystalline nanocomposites with varying degrees of crosslinking. • Elastoplastic behavior featuring strain hardening emerges. • The strain hardening is rationalized considering the role of superlattice dislocations and compaction phenomena. • FEM simulations validate the applicability of the proposed method. Supercrystalline nanocomposites (SCNCs) feature sophisticated nanostructures that unlock tunable multi-functionalities. However, their mechanical behavior is only starting to be explored, hampering their serviceability. The core aspect of a material’s mechanical behavior is its flow behavior, i.e. its stress–strain relationship. Obtaining this for small-scale nanostructured materials like SCNCs remains a challenge. Nanoindentation is a viable technique for mechanical testing, but the associated complex stress state makes translation into stress–strain curves non-trivial. Here, we propose a spherical indentation-based method for the extraction of uniaxial stress–strain curves solely from nanoindentation data, without additional tests nor numerical simulations. Finite-element simulations are, instead, employed for the validation of the proposed protocol, and a strain limit of 0.03 guarantees maximum accuracy. The obtained stress–strain curves of isotropic SCNCs with varying degrees of ligands crosslinking reveal an elastoplastic behavior featuring strain hardening, rationalized considering superlattice dislocations and compaction phenomena. Extremely high values of the yield strength and strain hardening exponent are found for crosslinked SCNCs. An indentation size effect is observed, resulting from the interplay of strain gradient plasticity and shear transformation-mediated plasticity. While paving the path for the development of SCNC, the proposed approach is easy to implement and applicable to a broad spectrum of materials.

title: Breathable, active antibacterial, and Ag/SiO2-enhanced daytime radiative cooling PLA nanofabric electronic for bio-protection and wireless health monitoring
abstract: • BCNF showed ultrahigh particle filtration efficiency of 99.96% for PM 0.3. • BCNF showed a high values of long-wave infrared emissivity (92.3%). • BCNF offered a average surface temperature drop of bare skin by 13.6 °C. • BCNF could wirelessly sense abnormal biological activities in real time. • BCNF showed killing rates of ∼ 100 % against E. Coli and S. aureus. In recent years, epidemics have shown a trend of high transmissibility, high pathogenicity, and summer transmission. This requires medical protective fabrics (MPFs) to improve their protective ability and thermal comfort during the summer and provide remote, real-time biomonitoring function. Herein, a smart, breathable, bioprotective composite nanofabric (BCNF) with high air filtration efficiency, excellent daytime radiative cooling ability, high antimicrobial activity, and a triboelectric biosensing function was prepared. BCNF was mainly consisted of bead-structured Ag nanoparticle/silica nanoparticle (SiO 2 NPs)-embedded poly-L-lactic acid (PLA) nanofibers and an intermediate conductive layer of Ag nanowires. The BCNF showed an increased radiative cooling ability of 112.5 % and an increased electrical output power of 171.4 % following the incorporation of Ag and SiO 2 . Besides, it also achieved the following properties: (i) good water resistance and moisture permeability (≥17.2 kPa; 3691.3 m 2 ·24 h); (ii) ultrahigh particle filtration efficiency of 99.96 % for PM 0.3; (iii) good biocompatibility; (iv) BCNF-covered skin temperature decreased by 13.6 °C compared to that covered by MPF; (v) strong antimicrobial activity with killing rates of ∼ 100 % against E. Coli and S. aureus at an Ag content of 500 mg/kg with 2 h contact; (vi) a wireless real-time biosensing ability to detect abnormal physiological activities, such as rapid breathing and coughing.

title: High-throughput refractory alloy design for additive manufacturing
abstract: Commercial implementation of higher strength refractory alloys has largely been hindered by their poor fabricability. Additive manufacturing (AM) may provide more opportunities to fabricate stronger refractory alloys, but discovering alloys that are amenable to the printing process without cracking remains a challenge. Here, utilizing a high-throughput methodology, the tendency for cracking during laser melting was evaluated in 595 alloys in the Nb-Zr-W alloy family. In this approach, discontinuous compositional gradients are fabricated using spark plasma sintering, streamlining the subsequent laser spot melting and automated correlative characterization efforts. By assessing compositional trends in crack severity, promising alloy design strategies to mitigate interstitial embrittlement, solid-state cracking, and solidification cracking emerge. The results presented here establish how AM can broaden the refractory alloy design space, and provide a suitable compositional library for the development of predictive criteria for cracking.

title: Multi-scale quality monitoring for laser additive remanufacturing: Example with surface continuity and hardness monitoring in ceramic reinforced metal matrix composite
abstract: • An innovative multi-scale quality monitoring method with a single sensor for comprehensive quality description of LARM-prepared PRMMCs. • A CRM-F model with lightweight single-path shared backbone and multi-task branch is proposed to predict comprehensive quality in LARM. • The mesoscopic surface continuity and macroscopic hardness is first predicted simultaneously for MMCs fabricated by LARM. Ceramic particle reinforced metal matrix composites (PRMMCs) fabricated by laser additive remanufacturing (LARM) provides a new route for the in-situ restore and surface enhancement of high value-added parts. However, the absence of an effective quality description method for LARMed PRMMCs hindered their application due to the complex multi-scale defects. This work presents promising results aim to develop an innovative multi-scale quality monitoring method for comprehensive quality description of LARM-prepared PRMMCs utilizing a single sensor. An innovative classification-regression multi-task framework with fully depth-separable convolutional backbone (CRM-F model) was introduced to simultaneously predict mesoscopic surface continuity and macroscopic hardness. The results show that the prediction results of the CRM-F model exceed 95 % accuracy on the surface continuity branch, and the prediction errors on the hardness regression prediction branch are stabilized within 5 %. Meanwhile, the CRM-F model with concise single-path architecture demonstrates excellent inference efficiency, and its inference time of 8.10 ms/frame provides an irreplaceable advantage for real-time monitoring on micro-industrial computers with Inter-CPUs. A prototype human–machine interfacing system developed on the basis of the CRM-F model lays a solid foundation for subsequent closed-loop control and digital twins in LARMed PRMMCs.

title: Recent advances in biogenic self-powered sensors: material, mechanism and application
abstract: • Comprehensive review on the integration of biopolymers (cellulose, chitosan, alginate, silk) into self-powered sensors, emphasizing their sustainability, biocompatibility, and tunable properties. • In-depth analysis of energy conversion mechanisms: moisture-enabled, thermoelectric, triboelectric, piezoelectric, and electromagnetic harvesting, with a focus on biopolymer-based systems. • Advanced material strategies including nanocomposite engineering, surface functionalization, and hierarchical structuring to enhance energy harvesting and sensing performance. • Diverse applications in wearable electronics, industrial monitoring, environmental sensing, and biomedical devices, demonstrating real-world viability of biogenic self-powered systems. • Future outlook highlights challenges and directions such as multiscale optimization, green manufacturing, extreme environment adaptation, and interdisciplinary integration for next-generation intelligent sensors. The rapid advancement of Internet of Things (IoT) and flexible wearable technologies is driving demand for miniaturized, sustainable, and self-powered sensors. Self-powered sensing which directly converts environmental stimuli such as temperature, humidity, and mechanical forces into electrical signals without external power. Biomass-based polymers (e.g., cellulose, chitosan, silk fibroin, alginate) have emerged as ideal platforms for next-generation self-powered sensors owing to their natural abundance, biodegradability, eco-friendliness, and tunable nanostructures. Crucially, these biopolymers not only generate electricity independently through triboelectrification and moisture-induced mechanisms but also form high-performance composites with inorganic nanomaterials. These hybrids significantly enhance mechanical robustness and power output while retaining inherent bio-sourced advantages. This energy-harvesting process intrinsically transduces target signals into electrical responses, enabling self-powered sensing. This review systematically examines fundamental biopolymer properties and the principles of harvesting humidity, thermal, and mechanical energy. It further explores surface modification and nanocomposite engineering strategies to achieve energy-harvesting and self-powered sensing capabilities. Finally, we outline future directions focusing on multiscale performance optimization via micro/nanostructural design, green scalable manufacturing, applications in extreme environments, and interdisciplinary frameworks, ultimately bridging self-powered technology with sustainable natural materials to advance the development of intelligent sensing in the future.

title: Bioactive chitosan/polycaprolactone cryogel sponge co-loaded with ciprofloxacin and ginger for controlled drug release and healing of infected wounds
abstract: Bacterial infections are a major challenge in wound management, emphasizing the need for advanced antibacterial dressings. In this study, we developed a ciprofloxacin (CIP) - and ginger extract-loaded chitosan lactate (Chit)/polycaprolactone (PCL) composite sponge designed for the treatment of Escherichia coli-infected wounds. The synergistic effects of CIP and ginger extract provided potent antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and pro-healing properties, while the Chit/PCL matrix acted as a bioactive scaffold. Chit/PCL sponges were fabricated in different ratios (Chit60/PCL40, Chit50/PCL50, and Chit40/PCL60) and characterized through ATR-FTIR, XRD, FE-SEM, contact angle measurements, and mechanical strength analysis. The Chit60/PCL40 formulation showed a highly porous structure (average pore size: 42.00±0.75 μm) with enhanced compressive strength (14% higher than pure chitosan sponges) and moderate hydrophilicity, which supported superior cell viability. The Chit60/PCL40/CIP/Ginger composite exhibited controlled CIP and ginger releases and demonstrated effective antibacterial activity. In vitro studies on fibroblast cultures confirmed non-cytotoxicity, while in vivo studies using an E. coli-infected rat model showed significantly accelerated wound healing with the incorporation of ginger. The multifunctional Chit60/PCL40/CIP/Ginger sponge effectively acted as both a bacterial barrier and a tissue regeneration promoter, offering a promising platform for advanced wound healing applications.

title: Experimental and simulation analysis of the influence of GNPs on the interfacial properties of CF/Epoxy − TA15 fiber metal laminates
abstract: This study investigates the effect of graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs) on the interfacial and mechanical properties of carbon fiber reinforced epoxy resin-based titanium alloy laminates (CF/Epoxy - Ti). Selective laser melting (SLM) was employed to in situ grow GNPs on Ti plates, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were conducted to explore the reinforcement mechanism. Experimental results revealed that SLM-treated Ti plates increased the shear strength of fiber metal laminates (FMLs) by 120% compared to untreated plates. Further, FMLs with 1.6 wt.% GNPs exhibited the highest shear strength (22.4 MPa), significantly surpassing untreated FMLs. Microscopic analyses and MD simulations demonstrated that GNPs enhance interfacial energy, thereby improving the mechanical properties of FMLs.

title: Research on the microstructure and properties of Cu-Ni-Si-Ti alloys with micro-nano hybrid systems
abstract: • Micron/nanoscale Ni 16 Ti 6 Si 7 and nanoscale Ni 2 Si precipitate in Cu-Ni-Si-Ti alloys. • Cu-Ni-Si-(Ti) alloys are mainly strengthened by fine nanoscale Ni 2 Si phases. • The micron Ni 16 Ti 6 Si 7 promotes the recrystallization nucleation of Cu. • Cu-4.84Ni-1.04Si-0.5Ti shows higher HDI stress from GNDs at G phase/Cu interfaces. The Cu-Ni-Si-Ti alloys with micron Ni 16 Ti 6 Si 7 phase and nano δ-Ni 2 Si dual-scale reinforcement particles were prepared and their microstructures, properties as well as strengthening mechanism were studied. It is found that micron-sized Ni 16 Ti 6 Si 7 particles (∼8μm) formed during alloy solidification, along with submicron Ni 16 Ti 6 Si 7 and Ni 2 Si precipitates (∼200 nm). This behavior differed from that observed in conventional Cu-Ni-Si alloys. After heat treatment, the micron and submicron Ni 16 Ti 6 Si 7 particles form semi-coherent interfaces with the α-Cu matrix, promoting recrystallization nucleation during hot rolling and thereby effectively refining the grain size of the alloy. Meanwhile, the nanoscale Ni 2 Si precipitates (∼30 nm) act as the primary strengthening phase, pinning grain boundaries and dislocations during deformation. Due to the significant elasticity modulus mismatch between Cu matrix and Ni 16 Ti 6 Si 7 phase, a large strain gradient during the tensile process will lead to HDI strengthening, and improve the overall performance of the material through the storage and induction of dislocations at the Cu grain boundaries and the Ni 16 Ti 6 Si 7 -Ni 2 Si/Cu interface. Therefore, compared with Cu-3.2Ni-0.7Si alloy, Cu-4Ni-0.9Si-0.5Ti alloy exhibits higher elastoplasticity while maintaining similar strength and conductivity. Its peak-aged conductivity reaches 35.0 ± 0 %IACS, with elastic modulus of 142 ± 4GPa, tensile strength of 747 ± 7 MPa, and elongation of 12.1 ± 0.3 %.

title: Hollow ZIF-8 nanoparticles Delivering PAH-ACP for multifunctional dentin Repair: Simultaneous Remineralization, antibacterial Activity, and Odontoinduction
abstract: • Hollow ZIF-8 loaded with PAH-ACP for adhesive interfaces. • Induction of the intrafibrillar mineralization of collagen fibrils. • Robust antibacterial activity and enhanced odontoinductive activity. • Demonstrates promising applications in adhesive dentistry and biomaterial design. Resin-bonded restorations, a prevalent treatment modality for dental defects, are prone to complications including nanoleakage, secondary caries, and pulpal pathology over extended service periods. To address these challenges, this study developed a multifunctional biomaterial, HZN@PAH-ACP, specifically designed for application at the dentin bonding interface. The material was fabricated by etching ZIF-8 with tannic acid to produce HZN, which was subsequently loaded with poly(allylamine)-stabilized amorphous calcium phosphate (PAH-ACP). The structure and formation mechanism of this biomaterial were thoroughly investigated using electron microscopy and molecular dynamics simulations. Meanwhile, HZN@PAH-ACP effectively induced intrafibrillar mineralization of collagen fibers and promoted remineralization of demineralized dentin, significantly reducing nanoleakage within the hybrid layer. Furthermore, the material inhibited the activity of Streptococcus mutans and exhibits excellent biocompatibility, while simultaneously enhancing the odontogenic differentiation and mineralization of human dental pulp stem cells. All powered by the simultaneous release of calcium, phosphate, zinc ions, and tannic acid, and the reduction in pH further accelerates this process. The development of this biocompatible, multifunctional repair biomaterial presents considerable clinical potential, as it addresses multiple challenges concurrently through a single application, that can be used in adhesive primers and pulp capping agents, offering a promising solution for dental restoration.

title: Nanotopography-driven changes in focal adhesion morphology of human dermal fibroblast cells on inkjet-printed hierarchically structured hemitoroids
abstract: Two-component polymer particle dispersions can be used to make nanostructured coatings with diverse applications. In this study, blends of polystyrene and acrylonitrile butadiene styrene latex dispersions were formulated for inkjet printing. When printed onto glass coverslips with a 50 µm drop spacing (DS) the result was ultrathin, nanostructured coatings. Increasing the DS to 100 µm produced arrays of nanostructured hemitoroids approximately 30–60 µm in diameter. By adjusting the blend ratio, the nanotopography of the hemitoroids could be tuned (e.g. S q 6–32 nm). These hemitoroid arrays, which exhibited different nanotopographies, were used for studying the influence of nanotopography on the morphology of focal adhesions (FAs) of human dermal fibroblast cells. Statistically significant differences in FA shape (e.g. roundness and aspect ratio) and size (area and perimeter length) were observed for different latex blends — even when the difference in RMS roughness (S q ) was only 3.9 nm. Strong correlations were observed between FA morphology and surface roughness in terms of S a , S q , S dr , S pk , and S k (R 2 ≥ 0.9 and Pearson’s r≥|0.95|), indicating that the response in FA morphology was mainly driven by nanoscale height variations and fine texture of these surfaces. These findings hence highlight the role of nanotopography in modulating substrate-cell signal transduction.

title: Data-driven modeling of AlSi10Mg mechanical properties: predictive approach to process parameters selection in laser powder bed fusion
abstract: • Data-driven and physics-informed modeling optimizes LPBF AlSi10Mg with high accuracy. • Bidirectional LSTM outperforms RNN/LSTM with < 10 % error and physics-aligned interpretations. • Symbolic regression balances parameter influence for transparent process optimization. • Robust generalization reduces costs and improves part performance in industrial applications. • Machine learning framework accelerates AlSi10Mg development for tailored LPBF properties. Data-driven methods for accelerated design and optimization of additively manufactured AlSi 10 Mg components based on the prediction of their mechanical properties are presented. The bidirectional long short-term memory demonstrates superior performance compared to symbolic regression, achieving maximum relative errors below 7.83 % using 5-fold cross-validation for all predicted mechanical properties. Despite the possibility of achieving accurate predictions, symbolic regression and random forest methods yield feature importances that conflict with established LPBF knowledge, suggesting sequence learning methods may be better suited for capturing the process’s complex relationships. The models, validated against experimental datasets, exhibit accuracy within 10 % of typical physical measurement tolerances, demonstrating their industrial applicability for rapid process parameter screening. This approach enables efficient exploration of the additive manufacturing process space and facilitates the design of components with tailored mechanical performance.

title: A gold-doped Thionin carbon nanozyme induces ferroptosis to boost chemo/photo-dynamic therapy
abstract: Schematic representation of Au-CDs with anti-tumor efficacy by self-enhanced CDT and PDT combination to mediate ferroptosis. • The gold doping increased the CAT-like and POD-like enzymatic activities of carbon dots, demonstrating strong chemo-dynamic therapy capability. • Au-CDs can act as highly efficient photosensitizers, capable of generating singlet ox-ygen with production rate as high as 1.46. • Au-CDs are able to deplete glutathione in TME and decompose H 2 O 2 in TEM, pro-ducing O 2 and ROS, thereby achieving more effective CDT and PDT. • Au-CDs release ROS in TEM, mediate oxidative stress, promote lipid peroxidation, and upregulate the expression of TFR1 to facilitate the influx of Fe 2+ , thereby enhancing the process of ferroptosis in tumors. Both reactive oxygen species (ROS) and ferroptosis are recognized for their pivotal regulatory roles in tumor survival. However, the hypoxic and high glutathione (GSH) environment within tumors presents a significant barrier to these therapeutic strategies. In this study, we have developed a novel gold-doped carbon-dotted nanozyme (Au-CDs) exhibiting multi-enzyme-like activities, which effectively alleviate tumor hypoxia and achieve the self-enhanced combined treatment effect of chemodynamic (CDT) and photodynamic therapy (PDT) independent of oxygen. Furthermore, it effectively depletes GSH to achieve a robust ROS amplifier. The synthesized Au-CDs have demonstrated efficacy in inducing ROS release, promoting lipid peroxidation accumulation and reducing the GSH levels, resulting in the inhibited proliferation of tumor cells in vitro . In a xenograft model, Au-CDs effectively inhibited the tumor growth of nude mice. In terms of molecular mechanism, Au-CDs were able to upregulate transferrin receptor 1 (TFR1) expression and increase the Fe 2+ content, and finally to induce the tumor related ferroptosis, which was more significant in combination with self-enhanced PDT. The biosafety assessment demonstrated Au-CDs had no significant toxicity in the major organs of mice. Taken together, these findings suggested Au-CDs as a novel and safe nanozyme have great potential to be utilized in combination therapies in cancer.

title: High energy absorption and deformation recovery of laser powder bed fused NiTi arched spiral lattices via hybrid structural design
abstract: • The arch − spiral lattice structure developed through a hybrid structural design strategy. • A hybrid structural design incorporating spiral features can effectively mitigate stress concentration. • Hybrid structural design can enhance the mechanical and functional performance of structures. In conventional NiTi alloy lattice structures, stress concentrations at the nodes during deformation frequently lead to localised deformation zones, surpassing the reversible strain limits and diminishing energy absorption capacity. To address this issue, this study introduces a novel Arch-shaped Spiral Lattice Structure (ASLS), fabricated via laser powder bed fusion (LPBF). This structure integrates spiral features with conventional Arch-shaped Lattice Structures (ALS) through a hybrid design strategy to mitigate stress concentrations. Finite element analysis indicates that the spiral feature effectively reduces stress concentration in the ALS and enhances its damage tolerance. Mechanical testing reveals that the ASLS achieves an energy absorption of 241.32 J and a specific energy of 16.62 J/g, representing improvements of 297.89 % and 166.35 %, respectively, over the ALS. Shape memory effect tests demonstrate that the ASLS exhibits only 0.449 % cumulative irreversible strain after 10 compression-thermal cycles, highlighting superior shape memory stability. This enhancement is attributed to the continuous geometric characteristics of the spiral structure, which enable coupled torsional and bending deformation. This work provides valuable insights into the development of high-performance, reusable NiTi lattice structures, broadening their applications in aerospace buffering, biomedical scaffolds, and other advanced engineering domains.

title: Vibration-assisted thermal bonding (VATB) of CF/PEEK thermoplastic composites: Influence of bonding parameters on the lap shear strength
abstract: Thermoplastic composites excel in fatigue and impact resistance compared to thermoset composites. Notably, they allow in-situ consolidation using Automated Fiber Placement (AFP), which reduces manufacturing costs and energy consumption. However, AFP’s short processing time poses challenges in achieving optimal bond strength. To address this, the current research introduces an innovative technique called vibration-assisted thermal bonding (VATB). This method combines material preheating with sub-ultrasonic vibration during bonding to enable rapid, high-quality consolidation. The simultaneous application of heat and vibration raises the material temperature to its melting point and reduces polymer viscosity, respectively. To evaluate the effect of frequency-dependent vibratory pressure on consolidation quality, a custom machine integrating electrical heating and vibratory pressure was developed. The study systematically investigates the influence of bonding parameters such as preheating time, mold temperature, holding time, consolidation pressure, and vibration frequency. Lap shear strength is used as the key metric for evaluation.
