We proposed a synergistic mechanism between precipitation-induced diffusion blocking and thermodynamic evolution, driving the contraction of the transition zone during aging. HRTEM confirms that aging significantly reduces the interfacial lattice mismatch, with the fusion boundary decreasing from 7.62 % to 1.32 %, and the phase boundary markedly decreasing from 21.43 % to 6.62 %, effectively alleviating stress concentration at the interface. After aging, the micropillar compressive yield strength increases by approximately 20 %, and plastic compatibility is enhanced, leading to a significant improvement in the weld quality. This study provides a theoretical basis for optimizing the thermal stability of dissimilar metal welded joints.

title: Enhanced phase segmentation of scanning electron microscopy images using U-Net with energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy-guided labelling
abstract: This study introduces a deep learning-based methodology that uses U-Nets for the semantic segmentation of Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) images of Solid Oxide Cells (SOCs). The objective is the identification of the four key phases in hydrogen SOC electrode (porosity, yttria-stabilised zirconia (YSZ), nickel (Ni), and nickel oxide (NiO)). While the database used for training is built using Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDS) maps to help label the SEM images using Random Forest classification, the model is trained to segment SEM images directly, without the need for EDS. The results show that the model achieves high segmentation accuracy on SEM images without any manual pre-labelling stepand demonstrates robustness to brightness variations, while challenges such as blur and zoom are addressed through sensitivity analysis. Additionally, a “sliding window” post-processing approach for segmenting large-scale images is used to reduce edge artefacts. The benefit of this approach is to provide an automatic workflow that does not require long EDS acquisitions or a time-consuming manual labelling procedure, offering a scalable solution for microstructural analysis of SOC electrodes. • U-Net trained with EDS-guided labels segments SEM phases with high accuracy. • Model achieves 90% accuracy, removing the need for EDS during mappings. • Deep learning analysis is 60 times faster than semi-manual segmentation. • Model outperforms EDS-based labels, correcting segmentation misclassifications. • U-Net shows sensitivity to blur, zoom, and acquisition conditions.

title: Microstructure evolution of molten zirconium oxidative solidification: Experiment and numerical simulation
abstract: • Molten zirconium oxidative solidification experiments in high temperature steam environment were conducted. • A molten zirconium oxidative solidification model based on the phase field method was developed. • The microstructure evolution mechanism and external influencing factors of the molten zirconium oxidative solidification process were studied. The high-temperature oxidation behavior of zirconium alloys is a major limitation to their high-temperature applications. The microstructural characteristics during the oxidative solidification process of molten zirconium significantly influence its oxidation kinetics. This study combines experimental and numerical simulation methods to investigate the microstructural evolution characteristics during the oxidative solidification of molten zirconium. High-temperature steam environment experiments are conducted to observe the morphology of oxidative solidification dendritic structures. A phase field model considering flow, heat transfer, and oxygen transport is developed. The model is verified using theoretical solutions and experimental results. Based on the developed model, simulation analyses of the oxidative solidification process of molten zirconium are conducted. The results indicate that the model can accurately simulate the growth of dendrites and the inhomogeneity of oxygen content during solidification. The influence of external macroscopic conditions on the microstructural characteristics of solidification is investigated. The results indicate that the oversaturation of the zirconium melt determines the driving force for oxidative solidification. Both excessively low and high oversaturation can form a relatively stable solid–liquid interface. Melt flow causes deviation of the oxidative solidification dendrites. As melt flow intensifies, the deviation angle of the dendrites gradually increases, and the width of the dendrites decreases.

title: Achieving balanced mechanical-corrosion properties in laser-welded Al-Mg-Si-Cu alloy welds by Ti content optimization
abstract: To overcome the trade-off between mechanical properties and corrosion resistance in laser-welded Al-Mg-Si-Cu alloy welds, this study investigates the effect of titanium content on the porosity, grain size, precipitated phases, mechanical properties, and corrosion behavior of laser-welded welds. The precipitation of Al3Ti/(Al, Si)3Ti in the weld acts as the heterogeneous nucleation sites, thereby significantly refining the grain structure, which improves the corrosion resistance. These Al-Ti phases also have a positive effect on the corrosion resistance of the weld, as the potential difference between them and the matrix is not significant. The increase in weld strength can be mainly attributed to grain refinement. An excessively high Ti content deteriorates the mechanical properties by increasing hydrogen solubility in the weld, thereby impeding hydrogen's escape from the molten zone. Overall, the welds achieve the best combination of mechanical properties and corrosion resistance when the Ti content is 0.60 wt.%.

title: Identification of the role of zinc in Sn–Cu solder and interfacial intermetallic growth through experimental results and phase-field simulations
abstract: This study investigates the microstructural evolution and interfacial phenomena in five Sn–Cu–Zn solder alloys, focusing on the impact of Zn addition (0–1 wt.%). The findings reveal that Zn destabilises the eutectic interface, inducing cellular morphologies with fine and coarse eutectic at cell centres, while CuZn intermetallic compounds (IMCs) form in the interdendritic regions. Remarkably, even trace Zn additions significantly influence the solidification dynamics by reducing undercooling and altering the growth mode of primary β-Sn. However, these trace amounts have limited impact on suppressing η-Cu₆Sn₅ and ε-Cu₃Sn interfacial IMCs or Kirkendall void formation on Cu substrates.A Zn content exceeding 0.8 wt.% is required to effectively suppress IMCs over long-term high- temperature exposure. Nevertheless, the presence of a thin γ-Cu₅Zn₈ layer (<100 nm) at the interface substantially alters the nucleation, growth kinetics, and morphology of the η-phase. Phase-field simulations support these findings, demonstrating qualitative agreement with experimental data. The simulations further explain how the γ-phase modifies diffusion gradients, affecting the growth and distribution of η and ε phases. This work highlights the critical role of Zn in controlling solder microstructure and interfacial IMC development, offering valuable insights for optimising high- temperature lead-free solder joints.

title: Inter-pass peening for residual stress control in additive manufacturing: validation using ultrasonic, X-ray and contour method
abstract: In this study, round-robin experiments were carried out to evaluate the effectiveness of inter-pass peening as an in-process residual stress (RS) mitigation technique for Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing (WAAM) of Ti-6Al-4V components. A newly developed method, Phased Array Ultrasonics for Residual Stress Measurement (PAURS), was evaluated for its capability to accurately characterise residual stress distributions. To validate PAURS, two established techniques, X-ray Diffraction (XRD), a non-destructive method, and the Contour Method (CM), a destructive technique, were employed. PAURS, particularly when implemented with Full Matrix Capture (FMC), demonstrated enhanced accuracy through improved data redundancy and outlier rejection. Results from PAURS and XRD showed good qualitative agreement with finite element models derived from CM data, despite some quantitative differences. Inter-pass peening was found to significantly reduce tensile RS in the heat-affected zone, with performance comparable to post-process peening. These findings support the use of inter-pass peening as an effective in-process RS mitigation strategy and highlight the potential of PAURS as a reliable, non-destructive RS measurement method for WAAM Ti-6Al-4V components.

title: Corrigendum to “Elucidating dislocation core structures in titanium nitride through high-resolution imaging and atomistic simulations”. [Mater. Des. 224 (2022) 111327]
Bioactive elastomeric composites based on poly(glycerol adipate urethane), bioactive glass, and anoplin-derived peptide for improved antimicrobial properties
abstract: • Elastomeric composites of poly(glycerol adipate urethane), bioactive glass, and antimicrobial peptide, for small bone defect regeneration, were developed to prevent nosocomial infections. • Nature-inspired antimicrobial peptide UG39, based on anoplin, as a component of composites, delivers a rapid response against S. aureus . • The concentration of UG39 immobilised on the poly(glycerol adipate urethane)/bioactive glass composite’s surface corresponds to minimal inhibitory concentration. • Poly(glycerol adipate urethane)/bioactive glass composites under application conditions (37 °C) are in a rubbery state with T g lower about 30 °C than the temperature of the working conditions. • The master curves of the storage and loss shear moduli at 37 °C confirm a wide frequency range of rubbery state, ensuring stable mechanical properties of the composites at service conditions. Three-component antimicrobial elastomeric composites based on poly(glycerol adipate urethane) (PGAU), bioactive glass particles, and nature-inspired peptide (UG39) were manufactured for applications in regeneration of small bone defects. Due to infections frequently accompanying surgical procedures of scaffold implantation, the composites are designed to prevent nosocomial infections. The UG39 mimicing anoplin − the antimicrobial peptide found in the venom sac of the solitary wasp Anoplius samariensis , was immobilised on the surface of the composites to ensure a rapid antimicrobial response to a possible bacterial infection. For long-term antibacterial properties strontium-doped bioactive glass was used. The influence of bioactive glass on linear viscoelastic properties of PGAU was estimated. The master curves of the storage and loss modulus and loss factor at a reference temperature of 37 °C were constructed. The rubbery plateau modulus was 3.91 MPa and 5.42 MPa for the composite with 10 wt% and 20 wt% of bioactive glass, respectively. For composites with 20 wt% of bioactive glass, a beneficial broadening of the frequency range of the rubbery state was observed compared to neat PGAU. UG39-loaded composites showed cytocompatibility in vitro and demonstrated antibacterial activity against S. aureus , including MRSA isolates, with a significant decrease in bacterial viability after 6 h of incubation.

title: Satellite-free droplet formation in material jetting via rheology-driven waveform modelling approach
abstract: Stable, satellite-free droplet ejection is essential for high-resolution material jetting (also known as 3D inkjet printing). Existing “printability windows” often fail to predict satellite formation accurately, as they neglect non-Newtonian fluid behaviour and waveform dynamics. This study presents a fast-track, experiment-driven approach to identify single-droplet waveform parameters, namely pulse width and driving voltage, from rheological data of polymer inks across different jetting temperatures, eliminating tedious drop-watching trials. Three UV-curable acrylate inks are systematically characterized for complex viscosity, viscoelasticity, relaxation time, dynamic surface tension, oscillation and damping behaviour, and density at five temperatures using a high-frequency squeeze-flow rheometer and bubble tensiometer. Cross, Hua & Rosen, Maxwell, Arrhenius, and Eötvös models are applied to extrapolate these properties to the inkjet regime (∼10 5 s −1 shear rate, <1 ms surface age). A correlation between droplet velocity and driving voltage, dependent on material properties, is established. Satellite formation is governed almost exclusively by droplet velocity, with distinct regimes: <3 m/s (no satellite), 3–3.8 m/s (one satellite). A general equation quantifying the relationship between droplet velocity and driving voltage enables predictive waveform design from rheological data. The methodology, validated with two UV-curable inkjet inks, accelerates the search for a satellite-free single droplet waveform.

title: Data-driven curation of organometallic precursor boiling points via natural language processing
abstract: The development of high-performance semiconductor devices relies on precise control of thin-film deposition techniques, notably Chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD) and Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD). Central to these processes are organometallic precursors, whose boiling points control volatility and vapor delivery conditions, thereby constraining processing windows and precursor feasibility. However, boiling point data for these precursors are scattered across unstructured literature and underrepresented in commercial databases. To address this gap, we developed a Natural Language Processing (NLP) pipeline to systematically extract, validate, and organize boiling point data from 5,442 peer-reviewed articles since 2000. Using the ChemDataExtractor toolkit, we curated 1,902 candidate data points, followed by rigorous multistage filtration to remove duplicates, non-standard nomenclature, non-organometallic compounds, and erroneous entries. The validated dataset comprises 75 organometallic precursors with boiling points from 21 °C to 181 °C. Comparative analysis with CAS Registry and SciFinder revealed that over 80 % of these data points were previously undocumented, underscoring the novelty of the dataset. This work demonstrates the utility of NLP-driven literature mining in building chemically precise databases and offers a scalable framework to accelerate precursor characterization and materials discovery in semiconductor manufacturing and ceramic thin-film applications.

title: The interaction between nanoscale MIL-53(Fe) and Fzd6 protein drives enhanced bone regeneration
abstract: The interaction between nanomaterials and biomolecules is pivotal in advancing biomedical applications, especially in bone tissue regeneration. While metal–organic framework (MOF) nanomaterials are widely used in bone tissue engineering, their interactions with biomolecules remain underexplored. This study utilized MIL-53(Fe), a MOF known for its structural stability and biocompatibility, to investigate its impact on osteogenesis through biomolecular interactions. Results indicated that MIL-53(Fe) significantly promoted osteogenesis in human bone marrow stromal cells (hBMSCs) by activating the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations revealed that MIL-53(Fe) had the highest binding affinity for the Fzd6 receptor, a key component of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway. This binding stabilized the Fzd6 protein, enhancing its structural dynamics and reducing conformational flexibility. These findings suggest that MIL-53(Fe)’s interaction with Fzd6 is crucial to its osteogenic effects. Additionally, MIL-53(Fe) promoted bone regeneration in a rat calvarial bone defect model, as confirmed by micro-CT and histological analyses. These results indicate the potential of MIL-53(Fe) as a novel nanomaterial for bone regeneration and provide new insights into nanomaterial-biomolecule interactions in osteogenesis.

title: Dual-component nanofiber scaffolds of silica and collagen for enhanced mechanical integrity and osteogenic bioactivity
abstract: Nanofiber scaffolds have gained significant attention as bone substitutes due to the high surface area and interconnected pore structure closely resembling the extracellular matrix (ECM), thereby supporting cell growth and promoting tissue regeneration. This study specifically focused on developing new electrospun scaffolds using silica and fibrillated collagen (SifCo), a key biopolymer in the natural bone matrix, targeting bone tissue engineering applications. The hybrid scaffolds were fabricated using a dual-nozzle electrospinning device equipped with two syringes, each separately filled with silica and collagen. Our findings demonstrated that the involvement of collagen nanofibers (NFs) within silica NFs significantly modifies silica-based scaffold characteristics, thus enhancing Young's modulus from 13±1 MPa for silica to 69±25 MPa for SifCo NFs and improving cell proliferation compared to pure silica scaffolds. Besides, these hybrid NFs showed a lower degradation rate (15.24± 4.75%) than their pure collagen NFs (83.44±12.95%) after 14 days, providing more sustained support for tissue growth. This combination of silica and collagen in the hybrid scaffolds benefited both materials' strengths while modifying their limitations. This balanced approach can offer an effective strategy for bone tissue replacements, potentially addressing the need for scaffolds that can provide both adequate stability and favorable biological properties.

title: Enhancing strength and ductility in ultrahigh-strength steel via flash-heated IQP with lamellar heterostructure and chemical heterogeneity
abstract: • A novel processing route combining full austenitization, intercritical quenching, and flash heating Q&P was developed. • The microstructure shows ferrite-martensite lamellar structure with Mn-induced chemical heterogeneity in martensite. • The sample shows greater retained austenite fraction and stability than conventional quenching and partitioning steels. • With 0.24 wt% C and 2.27 wt% Mn, the sample achieves an outstanding product of strength and elongation of 35.8 GPa·%. • The sample enhances both strength and ductility beyond traditional Q&P steels, breaking the strength-ductility dilemma. To develop ultrahigh-strength steel with both excellent mechanical properties and cost efficiency, this study integrates complete austenitization (CA), intercritical quenching (IQ), and flash heating quenching and partitioning (FHP). The resulting microstructure features a heterogeneous lamellar structure (HLS) of ferrite and martensite, along with chemical heterogeneity (CH) of the manganese (Mn) element within the martensite. The CA + IQ + FHP treatment imparts the steel with an exceptional strength-ductility synergy (YS: 1176 MPa, TS: 1868 MPa, TE: 19.2 %), which can be primarily attributed to the high density of geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs) and the alignment of dislocations in ferrite that is perpendicular to the interfaces between soft and hard phases, thereby inducing significant hetero-deformation induced (HDI) strengthening. Nanoindentation tests demonstrate that the CA + IQ + FHP sample exceeds the rule of mixtures (ROM) due to HDI strengthening, a finding further validated by loading–unloading-reloading (LUR) tensile tests. In comparison to conventional quenching and partitioning (Q&P) steels, the CA + IQ + FHP sample achieves a superior product of strength and elongation (PSE) of 35.8 GPa·% with low carbon (C) (0.24 wt%) and Mn contents (2.27 wt%). Although the transformation-induced plasticity (TRIP) effect is not activated, both the fraction and stability of retained austenite (RA) are greater than those observed in traditional Q&P steels.

title: A machine learning multitasking integrated framework and its derived [Mo]eq-[Fe]eq map for designing TRIP titanium alloys
abstract: • A high-precision multitasking integrated framework for TRIP titanium alloy design was developed. • The integrated framework is interpretability, enabling the identification of key influencing factors for the TRIP effect. • First proposed, the [Mo] eq -[Fe] eq map enables quick judgement of TRIP effect occurrence in titanium alloys. To enable rapid and accurate design of TRIP titanium alloys, an integrated multitasking framework based on the Stacking algorithm was developed, for the first time integrating the Sparrow Search Algorithm (SSA) to optimize hyperparameters in the framework. The SSA-Stacking framework exhibited satisfactory predictive accuracy on the test set and outperformed traditional base models. A TRIP titanium alloy Ti-5Mo-5 V-3Cr-3Al-2Nb (wt. %) was designed based on the SSA-Stacking framework. It was experimentally verified that the TRIP effect occurred after the alloy was solution-treated at 870 °C for 0.5 h, which in turn achieved a good strength-plasticity matching with a tensile strength of 864 MPa, a yield strength of 748 MPa, and an elongation of 28 %. To provide researchers with a more convenient semi-empirical method for designing TRIP titanium alloys, a [Mo] eq -[Fe] eq map was constructed based on the dataset, SSA-Stacking framework, and SHAP analysis. Researchers can directly utilize the [Mo] eq -[Fe] eq map established in this study to rapidly determine whether the TRIP effect can occur. The [Mo] eq -[Fe] eq map demonstrates higher accuracy than the traditional semi-empirical design methods. Further combined with interaction analysis between [Mo] eq , [Fe] eq , and solution temperature, this study provides quantitative guidance for optimizing the chemical composition and heat treatment processes in TRIP titanium alloy development.

title: Synthesis and properties of a highly reactive inorganic salt-based solder paste for 1060 aluminum alloy soldering
abstract: Aluminum alloy liquid-cooled plates are the most widely used heat management technology in high-end servers and aerospace thermal control systems. Due to the natural oxidation layer, welding and effective connection of aluminum alloys are still difficult, which greatly limits the performance and lifespan of welded components. In this study, highly active ZnCl 2 -SnCl 4 inorganic salt-based fluxes are prepared in three different proportions and mixed with SnAg3Cu0.5 alloy powder to obtain environmentally friendly solder pastes (LG-1, LG-2, LG-3). The viscosity, acidity, physical stability, and copper plate corrosion of the fluxes meet the standard requirements specified for high-quality soldering, and the three solder pastes had low wetting angles on the 1060 aluminum alloy. LG-3 exhibits the best mechanical properties, reaching a maximum tensile stress and tensile strength of 740.22 N and 38.01 MPa, respectively. Nanoindentation tests were conducted on the aluminum substrate, soft solder paste, and interface, and the results showed that LG-3 had the highest hardness. SEM and FIB-TEM reveal that the solder pastes and aluminum alloy are connected by an intermetallic compound layer. LG-3 has a relatively high ZnCl 2 content, which penetrates the Al grain boundaries during welding and generates Zn-Al IMCs, thus enhancing the mechanical performance of the welded joints.

title: Powder heat treatment for cold spray additive manufacturing: role of athermal omega and omega assisted α precipitation in β-Ti-5553 alloy
abstract: • Ti-5553 As-received powder develops athermal omega after one-cycle powder heat treatment. • Embrittlement of the thermal omega phase hinders dislocation movement during cold spray additive manufacturing deposition. • A two-cycle heat treatment powder produces omega-assisted fine alpha, improving deformability. • The porosity of the deposit decreases from around 14% to approximately 7% by using the two-cycle powder heat treatment. • After a two-cycle powder heat treatment, nano-hardness increases by around 34% compared to the As-received powder. Cold spray additive manufacturing (CSAM) enables sustainable repair by minimising thermal degradation. In this study, Ti-5553 powder was heat-treated to examine how nanoscale ω-phase precipitates and their role in promoting fine α precipitation within the β matrix affect its cold sprayability. In a one-cycle heat treatment (HT-1: 900 °C/3h), athermal ω precipitates (ω ath ) developed within the β matrix, as identified by selected-area electron diffraction (SAED). A two-cycle heat treatment (HT-2: 900 °C/3h + 665 °C/1h) dissolved ω ath and generated ω-assisted fine α precipitates, which are Widmanstätten intragranular α (α WM ). Splat morphologies and deposits were characterised by electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD), transmission Kikuchi diffraction (TKD), and electron channelling contrast imaging (ECCI). The HT-1 powder showed reduced deformability due to the presence of ω ath , while the HT-2 powder showed enhanced deformation, attributed to facilitated slip transmission by fine α WM precipitates. HT-2 powder deposits had reduced porosity (7%) compared to those from as-received (AR) powder (14%). The HT-2 powder showed increases in nanohardness of approximately 33.7% and 35.2% compared to the AR and HT-1 powders, respectively. This work highlights that precipitation engineering can optimise β titanium alloys for CSAM by uncovering how ω-assisted α WM precipitation governs deposition behaviour in Ti-5553.

title: Additive manufacturing of refractory high-entropy alloys: A critical review of fundamentals and advances
abstract: Refractory high entropy alloys (RHEAs) hold immense potential as superior alternatives to existing superalloys in the nuclear, energy, and aerospace industries. However, the fabrication of refractory alloys and RHEA parts has long been hindered by challenges associated with brittleness and a high oxidation rate. Fortunately, additive manufacturing (AM) presents a transformative opportunity for these materials. In contrast to conventional methods, AM offers the advantage of fabricating intricate and near-net-shape parts without restrictions caused by high melting points and severe high-temperature oxidation of refractories. Consequently, numerous studies have explored the feasibility of printing RHEAs for various applications, with the majority demonstrating improved mechanical properties and the ability to engineer microstructures and compositions. Nevertheless, challenges exist in the AM of these alloys, including the formation of microcracks, pores and elemental loss, impeding the realization of their full potential. This paper aims to delve into the fundamentals of RHEAs, encompassing the preparation of RHEA powders, the printability of these alloys and a critical assessment of their properties. To overcome the RHEA printing issues, this paper reviews the integration of thermodynamic modeling, phase diagram calculations, and numerical modeling, followed by an evaluation of the potential applications of RHEAs based on their properties and costs.

title: Roll‑to‑roll micro‑embossed carbonyl‑iron powder doped composite films with large‑area superhydrophobicity and microwave absorption
abstract: • A large-area superhydrophobic, wave-absorbing film based on micropatterned CIP doped PDMS was proposed. • The sedimentation of CIP during micro embossing process of the composite resin was explored. • Optimization of the static pre-curing was studied with the aim of improving wave-absorbing performance. • Large-area micropatterned CIP-doped PDMS film was achieved by roll-to-roll micro embossing process. Superhydrophobic, wave-absorbing multifunctional films hold considerable potential in the domains of anti-icing and stealth technology for unmanned aerial vehicles. However, existing multifunctional materials face limitations such as high energy consumption and the challenge of large-scale preparation. To address this problem, a large-area superhydrophobic, wave-absorbing multifunctional film made of carbonyl iron powder (CIP) doped poly(dimethylsiloxane) resin was proposed. The sedimentation behaviour of CIP within the resin during the micro-embossing process was explored, and effect of CIP dispersion on wave-absorbing performance was further studied. Furthermore, the static pre-curing step was optimized to improve CIP dispersion, thereby enhancing the hydrophobic and wave-absorbing performance. A large-area micropatterned CIP-doped composite film was achieved by employing a roll-to-roll micro embossing process. The film was demonstrated to exhibit a peak loss of −12.6 dB, an effective absorption bandwidth of 3.1 GHz, a water contact angle of 150.1°, a sliding angle of 9.6° and also excellent mechanical durability. The findings provide a technically feasible solution for the preparation of large-area superhydrophobic and wave-absorbing films, with application prospects in anti-icing and stealth technology.

title: Nanoparticle-mediated co-delivery of resveratrol and Mg2+ in an injectable hydrogel for multi-targeted repair of osteoporotic bone defects
abstract: Osteoporotic bone defects pose significant challenges for repair due to the excessive accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and an imbalance in bone regeneration. In this study, we developed a multifunctional delivery system named OCS-MSN@Res/Mg 2+ , which integrates mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSN) with a sodium alginate/oxidized carboxymethyl chitosan/silk fibroin composite scaffold (OCS). By forming a complex of Resveratrol (Res) with magnesium ions (Mg 2+ ) and subsequently coating it onto MSN particles, followed by embedding them into the OCS scaffold, the system achieves a coordinated controlled release of antioxidants and osteogenic metabolic promoters. In vitro experiments demonstrated that the system can efficiently scavenge ROS, activate the Nrf2/HO-1 pathway to enhance antioxidant defense mechanisms, regulate macrophage polarization toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype, promote osteogenic differentiation of Osteogenic cells (MC3T3-E1), and stimulate angiogenesis in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs). Furthermore, in vivo studies confirmed that this system significantly accelerates femoral defect regeneration in osteoporotic rats. Through its multi-effect synergy involving antioxidation, anti-inflammation, and osteogenesis, this innovative system not only optimizes the bone microenvironment but also enhances regenerative capacity. It provides a promising strategy with significant potential for clinical translation in the precise treatment of osteoporotic bone defects.

title: Grain boundary engineering for improved performance: A case study with Ni-superalloy on the hydrogen evolution reaction
abstract: • Grain boundary engineering has been employed for the first time in electrocatalysis. • Transfer of knowledge from Metallurgy to Catalysis led to activity-stability tradeoff. • Higher activity in engineered specimen is due to greater fraction of grain boundaries. • Higher stability in engineered specimen is due to greater fraction of Σ3 n boundaries. • Σ3 n boundaries restricted dissolution owing to its periodic nature. The present study investigates the impact of grain boundary engineering (GBE), a microstructural design strategy commonly employed in metallurgy to mitigate intergranular degradation, on the electrocatalytic performance of Ni-based alloys during the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). The GBE-treated specimen exhibits higher HER activity than the as-received (AR) condition, primarily due to its increased fractions of grain boundaries (GBs) and total number of triple junctions (TJs), which serve as additional catalytic sites and facilitate charge transfer. Operando dissolution measurements using a scanning flow cell (SFC) in conjunction with inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) reveal that, despite the enhanced activity, GBE-treated specimens show reduced dissolution compared to the AR condition. This improvement is attributed to a higher proportion of low-Σ coincidence site lattice (CSL) boundaries (Σ3 n (n ≤ 3); 79 ± 4 % in GBE vs. 55 ± 2 % in AR). Due to their higher periodicity, these boundaries are more resistant to dissolution, resulting in improved stability. These findings demonstrate that tailoring grain boundary character through GBE can result in a favorable balance between activity and stability, offering a promising approach to microstructural optimization in electrocatalysis.

title: Improving the energy and physical-mechanical characteristics of armor-protective elements of a new design
abstract: This study focuses on the improvement of multilayer armor-protective elements that integrate high-hardness materials, viscoelastic layers, and porous components to optimize energy dissipation and impact resistance. A mathematical model for numerical simulation of the damage process of armor-protective elements was developed, including an iterative procedure for defining material behavior in the Ansys/AutoDYN system. Convex multilayer armor structures were manufactured using explosive welding (steel–aluminum–steel; titanium–aluminum–titanium), and their ballistic resistance was evaluated through standardized NIJ 0101.06 tests. Numerical simulations demonstrated up to 70 % energy dissipation and a 5–6-fold reduction in damaging effect compared to flat layered armor. Experimental ballistic testing confirmed the feasibility of the proposed elements: neither 5.56 × 45 mm NATO nor 7.62 × 39 mm MSC projectiles penetrated the multilayer structures. Back-face deformation values remained below 3 mm, significantly lower than NIJ standards, validating both protective efficiency and structural integrity. The study confirms that convex multilayer armor elements produced by explosive welding provide enhanced ballistic resistance through combined mechanisms of plastic deformation, viscoelastic energy absorption, and geometric deflection. These findings support the practical application of the proposed structures in military vehicles, protective vests, and security systems, and open directions for future research on adaptive armor systems.

title: Construction of bi-layered osteochondral structures using DLP bioprinting with multi-component comprised bioink
abstract: Osteoarthritis is the most common chronic degenerative joint disease worldwide. Effective treatment of osteochondral defects requires multifunctional constructs with mechanical properties that support regeneration of both cartilage and subchondral bone. Such constructs demand bioinks with both osteogenic and chondrogenic capacities, as well as fabrication methods capable of producing multilayered structures that mimic the architecture and function of native osteochondral tissue. In this study, we aimed to develop: (1) multifunctional region-specific alginate-based bioinks incorporating α-tricalcium phosphate (α-TCP), RGD peptide, and N-cadherin peptide to enhance targeted cell differentiation, and (2) an integrated fabrication methodology for generating bi-layered osteochondral constructs. Methacrylated alginate (MA)-based bioinks were fabricated into bi-layered constructs via digital light processing (DLP) bioprinting, and the activity of the encapsulated cells was evaluated. The upper chondrogenic layer incorporated N-cadherin peptide to preserve a stable chondrogenic phenotype, while the lower osteogenic layer containing RGD peptide and α-TCP enhanced osteogenic activity and mechanical properties. The resulting integrated bi-layered constructs demonstrated distinct region-specific biological activities and structural integrity, indicating their feasibility for osteochondral tissue regeneration.

title: Effects of temperature and welding heat input on abnormal grain growth in friction-stir welds of 2219 aluminum alloy
abstract: Abnormal grain growth occurring during post-weld heat treatment deteriorates the mechanical properties of friction stir-welded joints. This study investigates abnormal grain growth behavior at different temperatures in 2219 aluminum alloy welds produced under various welding parameters. The underlying mechanisms were analyzed using quasi-in-situ EBSD, a modified Humphreys’ model, and cellular automata simulations. Results indicate that the mean size of the largest abnormal grains in the stir zone peaks at a critical temperature, which increases from 733 K to 783 K as the rotational speed rises from 800 rpm to 1600 rpm. At 808 K, abnormal grains exhibit lower mean dislocation density and Zener pinning than normal grains, with these differences amplified by lower temperatures or higher welding heat inputs. Projecting the modified Humphreys’ criterion into a 3D parameter space reveals that elevated temperatures increase the proportion of abnormal grains by reducing Zener pinning. Conversely, a higher welding heat input decreases abnormal grain number by increasing the initial grain size. The cellular automata model successfully captures the competitive growth dynamics among abnormal grains, providing mechanistic verification of the experimental observations and enabling analysis of key factors governing abnormal grain growth evolution under varying thermal conditions.

title: Spider silk-inspired dual-crosslinked bioadhesive for wet tissue adhesion
abstract: Clinical applications urgently require hydrogel-based bioadhesives with strong wet adhesion. Catechol-based hydrogels, inspired by mussel adhesion mechanisms, have previously demonstrated excellent wet adhesive performance. However, their intrinsically amorphous polymer chains and loose three-dimensional networks result in poor overall mechanical strength, which constrains further improvement of wet adhesion. In contrast, spider silk derives its outstanding mechanical properties from a unique hierarchical structure of interlaced β-sheet nanocrystalline and amorphous domains. Drawing inspiration from spider silk, we developed a biomimetic dual-crosslinked hydrogel (pTS). In this design, the β-sheets of silk fibroin (SF) mimic crystalline domains, while covalent bonds in poly(tannic acid) (pTA) and hydrogen bonds with SF emulate amorphous regions. This architecture yields a dual-crosslinked network with hydrogen bond-mediated physical and covalent bond-driven chemical crosslinks. By introducing tannic acid (TA) self-polymerization as a tunable parameter, we elucidated how the degree of polymerization regulates the hydrogel’s mechanical and adhesive properties. Notably, the pTS hydrogel exhibited markedly enhanced wet adhesion strength—more than twice that of the conventional TS hydrogel counterparts—reaching 60.13 kPa. In vivo, pTS accelerated wound closure, significantly increasing the healing rate by nearly 20 % over the control group. This work proposes a biomimetic strategy for engineering high-performance wet bioadhesives.

title: A 3D-printed composite scaffold with sequential release of graphene oxide/hydroxyapatite synergistically enhances angiogenesis-osteogenesis for bone defect repair
abstract: Angiogenic and osteogenic factors coordinate bone repair through time-dependent regulation of cellular responses, ensuring synchronized neovascularization and osteogenesis. Therefore, we designed a framework using polycaprolactone (PCL) and hydroxyapatite (HAp), which was then filled with a gelatin (GEL) matrix containing graphene oxide (GO) (PH/GO scaffold). The GEL matrix rapidly degrades in the early stage, releasing GO to enhance the migration of vascular endothelial cells and promote the expression of angiogenic factors to stimulate early angiogenesis. The continuous release of HAp from the PCL framework promotes osteoblast differentiation by enhancing expression of bone-specific proteins and matrix mineralization. In vivo studies confirmed that PH/GO-1 (1%GO) significantly elevates the expression of early angiogenic factors and accelerates new bone formation during defect healing. This scaffold synergistically enhances angiogenesis and osteogenesis via spatiotemporal release, demonstrating superior regenerative capacity. It enables sustained delivery of key bioactive molecules, offering a promising biomaterial strategy for critical-sized bone defect repair.

title: Innovative magnetic materials in tissue engineering: A review on revolutionizing regenerative strategies
abstract: Innovative magnetic materials are revolutionizing tissue engineering by enabling unprecedented remote and spatiotemporal control over regenerative processes. This research review systematically synthesizes cutting-edge advances in the field, highlighting the pivotal role of these materials as dynamic platforms for targeted therapy, controlled mechano-transduction, and mild thermal stimulation. Moving beyond conventional classifications, we delve into next-generation systems including high-performance superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPIONs), magneto-responsive hydrogels with tunable viscoelasticity, and 4D-printed shape-memory alloys. The analysis critically examines advanced characterization techniques that link material properties to biological function, as well as innovative design strategies for creating biomimetic scaffolds that facilitate on-demand drug delivery and guided cell differentiation. Furthermore, we document their transformative applications in enhancing the regeneration of complex tissues, such as bone, nerve, and cartilage, and demonstrate significantly improved healing outcomes in preclinical models. Finally, the review outlines the current translational challenges and future trajectories, emphasizing the development of integrated multi-functional platforms and scalable manufacturing processes. Thus, this work serves as a foundational, forward-looking resource to accelerate the clinical translation of next-generation magnetically driven therapies in regenerative medicine.

title: NIR laser triggered carbon monoxide, type I photodynamic and photothermal synergistic treatment of bacterial infected wounds
abstract: Bacterial infections stand as one of among the most common challenges encountered during wound healing. Although antibiotics have been employed to treat bacterial infections, the overuse and abuse of antibiotics has emerged as a significant global public health and societal concern, posing a serious threat to human health. Hence, the present study introduces a photo-responsive multifunctional nanoplatform (TCO NPs) that integrates type I photodynamic therapy (PDT), photothermal therapy (PTT), and carbon monoxide (CO) gas-based therapeutic modalities for the treatment of bacterial infected wounds. This multifaceted nanoplatform comprises a near-infrared (NIR) absorbing photosensitizer (TDNH) and a metal-free CO donor (3-HF). Upon irradiation with 808 nm laser, TCO NPs generate type I reactive oxygen species (ROS) and induce hyperthermia, effectively eradicating bacterial pathogens. Additionally, the ROS produced by TDNH triggers the controlled release of CO gas, which not only enhances antibacterial efficacy but also modulates inflammatory responses to facilitate tissue regeneration. Notably, this nanoplatform demonstrates a remarkable bacterial elimination rate exceeding 99 % in a full-thickness skin defect infection model under 808 nm laser exposure, underscoring its potential as a reliable approach for CO-enhanced PTT and type I PDT in the treatment of bacterial infected wounds.

title: Effect of welding wires on the microstructures and mechanical properties of TIG-welded Al-Cu-Mg alloys
abstract: Welding wire composition and porosity defects are two key factors affecting the performance of aluminum alloy welds. In this study, three commercial wires (ER2319, ER4043, ER5356) and TIG welding with/without pulse mode were employed to weld 2024-T4 alloy, aiming to clarify the scientific basis for matching wire composition to the base material (BM), reveal mechanisms of porosity reduction, weld strengthening, and fracture, and achieve low-cost and high-performance welding. Wire composition significantly influences its compatibility with the BM by altering the type and content of solute atoms, eutectic phase fraction, and grain size, with ER2319 wire achieving the optimal solution strengthening effect, the least amount of eutectic phase, and the smallest grain size, leading to a tensile strength of ∼340 MPa and an elongation of 6.8 %, with performance superior to ER4043 and ER5356. Pulse mode reduces porosity defects by stirring the molten pool and suppressing the formation of columnar crystals, decreasing the porosity by 92.69 % to 0.11 % and thereby increasing the elongation by 240 %. In addition, strain localization causes the weakest weld zone (WZ) to determine the elongation of joints, while the eutectic phase and porosity can accelerate joint failure, resulting in a severe reduction in the elongation.

title: Microstructure and wear resistance of Inconel 718 alloy coating repaired by microwave heating remanufacturing
abstract: A novel microwave heating remanufacturing (MHR) technology is proposed in this paper, and the Inconel 718 nickel-based superalloy coating is successfully prepared at the groove of substrate. The MHR coating shows the low porosity with only 2.8 % and its microstructure has gradient distribution feature, in which the upper layer is dominated by dendrites, and a large number of chromium carbide hard phases appear in this region. The middle layer of the powders undergoes four microwave heating stages of “micro-melting, necking, liquefaction, filling” to form cellular crystals, accompanied by a large number of quasi-continuous network-like carbide precipitation as the enhanced skeleton. The lower layer produces the chain-like Laves phase under the effect of heating. In addition, the microhardness of the MHR coating also shows the gradient distribution, gradually decreasing from 232 HV at the top to 210 HV at the bottom. The friction and wear experiments show that the average friction coefficient, the mass loss and the wear rate of MHR coating are 0.62, 7.1 mg, and 27.61 × 10 -6 mm 3 /(N·m), respectively, indicating the wear resistance is improved by more than 50 % compared to the substrate. The surface worn morphology shows that the dendrites on the top of MHR coating can withstand large normal load and transverse shear force. Besides, the fish-scale layered structure formed after dendrites bending can play a role of storing wear debris, which greatly improves the wear resistance of coating. The proposed MHR technology offers a completely new approach for the repair of parts and components.

title: Microstructure, impact reactivity, and damage effectiveness of 31W-29Mo-30Zr-7Ni-3Fe energetic structural materials
abstract: Energetic structural materials (ESMs) combine load-bearing capacity with energy release, offering multifunctional potential in impact and energy conversion applications. In this work, a 31W–29Mo–30Zr–7Ni–3Fe ESM was fabricated via powder metallurgy to enhance energy efficiency and damage effectiveness under high-velocity impact. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), quasi-static compression, and shock-induced reaction tests were conducted. The ESM exhibited a peak exothermic temperature of 569.7 °C and a heat release of 3380.2 J/g. Under impact loading, quantitative results showed that for flat-headed projectiles, peak chamber pressure increased from 0.13 MPa to 0.26 MPa and reaction efficiency from 15.56 % to 31.29 % as velocity rose from 643 m/s to 842 m/s. In contrast, spherical-headed projectiles achieved slightly lower values (0.16–0.25 MPa, 18.93–29.12 %) under comparable velocities. The material exhibited high compressive strength (≈1.22 GPa) and demonstrated excellent damage and ignition capability in target and fuel tank tests. Microstructural and phase analyses revealed that energy release is governed by sequential intermetallic formation and oxidation reactions. These results confirm the strong coupling between mechanical integrity and energetic response, underscoring the potential of W–Mo–Zr–Ni–Fe alloys for advanced reactive structural applications.

title: Recycling aged bitumen using bio-based rejuvenator tall oil: A molecular perspective on fusion, deagglomeration, and regeneration
abstract: The regeneration of asphalt pavements is essential for advancing green, circular, and sustainable transport infrastructure. A major challenge lies in the reverse design of rejuvenators tailored to the aging mechanisms of bitumen, particularly in selecting effective bio-based alternatives and understanding their molecular interactions with asphaltene aggregations. This study compares a bio-based rejuvenator, tall oil (T-type), with a conventional aromatic oil rejuvenator (A-type). Rheological tests evaluated the high- and low-temperature performance of regenerated binders, while atomic force microscopy and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy examined microstructural morphology and functional groups. To bridge macroscopic and microscopic observations, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and quantum chemical analyses were conducted. Results show that T-type molecules exhibit larger dipole moments and more heterogeneous surface electrostatic potential distributions than A-type rejuvenator, leading to stronger molecular polarity. This enhances affinity with asphaltene aggregations, enabling non-bonded interactions that disrupt π–π stacking and effectively increase stacking distances. With excellent diffusion efficiency, compatibility, and deagglomeration capacity, the T-type rejuvenator demonstrates superior regeneration effectiveness and surface repair of aged bitumen compared with A-type. These findings provide mechanistic insight and methodological guidance for reverse design of bio-based rejuvenators and support their selection in sustainable asphalt recycling.

title: Development of in-house PC/ABS blends and optimization of printing parameters for material extrusion method
abstract: In the field of Additive Manufacturing (AM) with Material Extrusion (MEX) technology, polycarbonate (PC) and acrylonitrile butadiene styrene (ABS) are two widely used thermoplastics, each offering distinct advantages. Standalone PC possesses high strength and thermal resistance but suffers from poor printability, whereas ABS offers good processability but lower mechanical performance. Herein, aiming at balancing their advantages, in-house blends with varying PC/ABS ratios were developed. Specifically, optimal set of parameters (heat zones temperatures, screw speed, fan speed) has been determined to produce filaments from each blend at different ratios. Additionally, a statistical Design of Experiments (DoE) approach based on the Taguchi method was employed to identify optimal set of printing parameters (layer thickness, nozzle temperature, print speed) and their significance on ultimate tensile strength. From this analysis, layer thickness was found to have a considerable influence on the ultimate tensile strength across most material combinations, while nozzle temperature only in some blends. Printing speed showed no statistically significant effect. Furthermore, samples printed using the optimal parameter combinations were evaluated through tensile testing, three-point bending, hardness, and impact testing. Fractographic analysis was also conducted to better understand the fracture mechanisms of the different material blends.

title: Biomaterial-based oral repair membranes: current advances, functional attributes, and future directions
abstract: Oral repair membranes, as biomaterials specifically engineered for the oral environment, demonstrate considerable promise for treating prevalent oral conditions such as pulpitis, tooth loss, oral mucosal defects and periodontal disease. These conditions inflict not only pain and functional impairment on patients but also impose substantial socioeconomic burdens. By providing a protective barrier over damaged oral tissues, these membranes facilitate a conducive environment for regeneration, thereby aiding the recovery of morphological and functional integrity. However, existing reviews have predominantly concentrated on periodontal barrier membranes, leaving the systematic summarization of repair strategies for the dental pulp and oral mucosa significantly underrepresented thus far. Although recent reviews have enhanced understanding in these two application areas, this paper provides a systematic overview. This review article meticulously examines the composition, functional characteristics, and clinical applications of various materials used for the regeneration of periodontal tissues, pulp, and oral mucosa.

title: Effect of ZrO2 and CuO nanoparticles on corrosion-induced Sn whisker grwoth from SnAgCu alloys: An experimental and quantum mechanical study
abstract: Composite solder joints were produced from 99Sn0.3Ag0.7Cu (SAC0307) solder alloy doped with ZrO 2 nano-powder and nano-fiber, and CuO nano-powder in 0.25 and 0.5 wt%. The samples were kept for 4000 h in an 85 °C/85RH% temperature-humidity test to enhance the corrosion-induced Sn whisker growth. SEM investigations revealed that ZrO 2 had a positive effect, while CuO had a negative effect on the corrosion susceptibility and corrosion-induced Sn whisker growth. A correlation was found between the grain refinement and the increase in corrosion susceptibility of the composite solder joints. Quantum mechanical study showed that ZrO 2 =Sn has lower binding energy than the Sn-Sn grain-boundary cohesion, and it could be advantageous, since then debonding occurs more likely under stress, thereby dissipating local strain and suppressing anisotropic deformation such as whisker growth. Coupling Sn with ZrO 2 that possesses d-orbitals at the valence band could yield a stable interface, even though a lattice mismatch exists between them. In addition, d-orbitals can distribute the corrosion-induced charges more uniformly across the surface, creating an electric field barrier effect that may counteract corrosion.
